His two feet are placed together as he sits upright upon a red lotus flower.
Below that, there are two bodhisattvas sitting side by side.

The latter bodhisattva is yellow in color throughout his body; he wears a golden flower crown upon his head, has a circular halo of blue light, and white rings on his ears, with white floral scarves draped over his shoulders.
The right arm is bent over the right knee with the palm extended outward, grasping the object resembling a boot-scraper held in the hands of the Bodhisattva before him.
The right arm is bent forward and held upright; the ring finger is bent, while the thumb, index finger, and little finger are held erect.
Upon his body he wears a yellow flower-patterned skirt and sits in the *hukuei* (half-lotus) posture upon a red lotus flower.

Next, the preceding Bodhisattva is entirely yellow in color; his head is adorned with a crown of small yellow chrysanthemums, and in his right ear there is a white jewel earring. He turns his face backward, appearing as if in the act of conversing with the Bodhisattva behind him.
Her breasts were large and prominent, draped with a light white cloth over her shoulders.
Her right arm was bent, extending outward to grasp a yellow object; this object resembled a severed rope, with small chrysanthemums attached at both ends to form a garland that hung downward.

The left arm is bent and placed upon the heart with the palm facing outward; the thumb and index finger are pressed together, while the middle and ring fingers are both bent, and the little finger is held straight upright.
Wearing a skirt of morning clouds, he sits with legs crossed upon a blue lotus flower.

The side-figures of this image are set against a green background; on both sides above the image, within blue clouds, are depicted the gods of the Śrotāpanna stage, each holding a floral garland in their two hands, which they drape downward to approach the image as an offering.
On both sides of the image are *pāṭala* trees and mountain shapes; beneath the lotus seat of the image is a jeweled pond.

Next, on the right side, there is a small youth wearing a flower crown, his entire body yellow in color, draped with a multicolored sash of various silks. He sits in a formal kneeling posture, bringing a flower garland to assist in the offering.

1. The Vajrarāja Sarvadṛṣṭadharma-mudrā Mantra, First. "Turn the palm of the right hand upward and press it against the back of the left palm. Then, cross the right thumb over the underside of the left little finger, and cross the left thumb over the top of the right little finger. Bring the backs of the hands together, extend the remaining three fingers straight, and let them touch the backs of the hands."
The mantra is:
“Oṃ vajra pabaya svāhā. This is the dharma-seal mantra;
if one performs the vajra rites, one should first make offerings with this dharma, and all vajras will be filled with joy.

2. The Dharma-Seal Mantra of the Great Mind of Vajragarbha, Part Two. "Cross the two ring fingers like hooks, placing them within the palms with the right over the left. Join the palms, extend the two middle fingers and the two little fingers straight upward so that their tips touch, slightly bending them. Open the two index fingers, and extend the two thumbs straight upward, side by side."
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye | Mahāyakṣasenāpate | Oṃ vajracaṇḍa sarvatuṣṭānandaka hana daha paca svidha huṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ. This dharma-seal mantra is named the Vajragarbha Great Mind Dharma-Seal Mantra; it is to be employed for all purposes.
"If a person wishes to practice the Vajra Dharma, they should first form this mudrā and recite the mantra to protect their body; then they will be fearless in all circumstances.

When treating all demonic illnesses, seasonal epidemics, or pestilential diseases affecting cattle, horses, and other livestock, one should construct a large water mandala outside the city gate. At the center of the mandala, place a large water jar—capable of holding four or five *sheng*—filled with pure water, and apply this mudrā and mantra one hundred and eight times."
At the four corners of the altar, place four plates of food; scatter various kinds of flowers along the four sides of the altar.
To the left and right of the altar, erect a pillar each; extend a single cord horizontally across the top of each pillar, and suspend a branch of green willow from the cord.

Arrange one seat along the edge of the left pillar; the mantra-practitioner sits upon it and recites the mantra. All food and drink within the mandala should be lifted up and discarded. Move the water-jar to the base of the pillar and drive the afflicted oxen and horses across the center of the mandala.

The mantra-master takes a willow branch and recites the mantra over it; using the branch, he sprinkles water from the vessel in succession upon the bodies of the oxen and horses, and their illness is immediately cured.

3. The Mantra and Mudrā for the Boundary-binding of Vajragarbha, Part Three: "Interlace the four fingers of both hands, hooking the right over the left; then, with each thumb, press down upon the nail of its respective ring finger."
The mantra is:

“Oṃ, kīli kīli, vajrayakṣa, bandha bandha, hūṃ, haḥ. This is the dharma-seal mantra; if one performs the Vajra rites, one should employ this seal-mantra to bind the boundary and provide protection before performing the ritual, whereby one shall be fearless in all respects.

If one uses this mantra-seal (dhāraṇī-mudrā) to consecrate ashes, water, white mustard seeds, or the like, they must all be struck with the seal; one may recite the mantra three times or seven times, and it shall be effective in all such cases.

If all evil spirits and ghosts in the four directions, as well as above and below, are to be dispersed and driven away, one should subsequently form the aforementioned seal and again perform the boundary-binding.

Rising, face directly toward the east; from the left side of the body, stand with the tip of the left foot forward, then place the right foot across the heel of the left, walking in a clockwise direction in the shape of a "T."

Each time they reached a meeting point or a circuit, at the gates, their heads would assume the fierce posture of a great Vajra; with wrathful eyes and bared fangs, their faces took on an expression of rage.
Having thus performed three circumambulations, one should subsequently bind the boundary again using the Great Body Method of Kuṇḍalī;

this constitutes the accomplishment of the rite. 4. The Dharma-Seal of the Dharmakāya Vajragarbha, the Fourth; also known as the Five-Spoked Seal. "Reverse the two ring fingers and place them within the palms, with the right pressing upon the left. Join the palms, extend the two middle fingers and the two little fingers straight upward so that their tips touch, slightly curve the two index fingers and attach them to the sides of the middle fingers, and extend the two thumbs straight upward side by side. The mantra for the movement of the index fingers is the same as the previous body-protection mantra."

"This is a single Dharma-seal. If there is anyone who upholds the Vajra-dharma, bathes daily, puts on fresh and clean robes, and performs this seal while reciting the aforementioned protection mantra, making offerings before the Buddha to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, then all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will constantly give rise to joy. They will cause all the Vajras of the ten directions to constantly come to provide empowerment and protection, assisting the practitioner’s strength."

5. The Vajragarbha-hṛdaya-dharmamudrā-mantra, Fifth. "Interlace the index fingers of both hands; place the four fingers below them within the palms. Extend the left thumb straight out, and bend the right thumb into the palm. Join the wrists."
The mantra is:

"Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa samayakrodha svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one wishes to perform any Vajra-rites, first invite the Vajra to be seated; then, having performed this seal and recited the mantra, all who perform the Vajra-rites shall obtain efficacy.

6. The Mantra of the Vajragarbha Flower-Sprinkling Dharma-Seal, Part Six: "Place the two forearms side by side. With the two thumbs, each press upon the tips of the two little fingers. Bring the sides of the heads of the two ring fingers together so they touch. Extend the two middle fingers and the two index fingers straight forward, held apart and not touching one another."
The mantra is:

“Oṃ vajra pūjaye svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one wishes to make offerings to the Vajras but lacks incense or flowers, one should form this seal and recite the mantra; then all the Vajras will be fully delighted.

7. The Vajragarbha Kilikīla Dhāraṇī Mudrā Mantra. This seventh [section] is also called the Subhā Mudrā Mantra; in the Tang language, it is called "Mudrā King. [Method: Interlace the two little fingers behind within the palms. Straighten the two middle fingers so that their tips touch each other. Bend each of the two index fingers back against the backs of the middle fingers, leaving a distance of about one finger-width from them without touching. Align the two thumbs and each grasp the middle joint of the middle finger. Move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is:

“Oṃ suṃbha niḥ suṃbha hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one can daily perform this mudrā and recite this mantra before the Buddha or at a site of practice (*bodhimanda*), one will always cause all Vajras to rejoice.

"When the offerings have been completed and all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have been dismissed, the mantra-practitioner shall take a small amount of ash with the thumb and ring finger of his right hand and recite the mantra over it seven times. He should then apply it to the crown of the head, the left and right shoulders, the heart, the neck, the space between the eyebrows, and the hairline; this is called 'protecting the body. Thus, one will be free from all fear, and no ghosts or spirits shall be able to approach the person."
Furthermore, this seal cures all diseases caused by ghosts.

When about to lie down to sleep, one should wash the hands and rinse the mouth, then immediately recite the mantra of this seal twenty-one times. One who protects themselves with this seal while lying down will have nothing to fear at all in the place where they sleep at night.

"If a person dreams at night of engaging in sexual intercourse with a woman and emits impurity, they should take thread of five colors and fashion a mantra-cord, reciting the mantra once for each knot; having thus tied one hundred and eight knots, they should put on a new, clean garment and fasten the aforementioned mantra-cord around their waist. By reciting the mantra to protect themselves while lying down to sleep, such an occurrence will no longer happen."
Furthermore, one employs this method to perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
Moreover, by performing this rite, all shall rejoice. Chapter Eight:

The Mantra-Seal of the Vajragarbha King of Mantras Cross the two little fingers behind so they rest in the palms; join the two middle fingers upright with their tips touching; slightly bend the two index fingers so that each rests upon the back of its respective middle finger, the tip positioned against the back of the third phalanx of the middle finger without touching it even slightly; join the tips of the two thumbs to press down on the second phalanx of the middle fingers; then move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is:

“Oṃ supoṣiddhakara rākṣasa svāhā. If a mantra-practitioner, when performing all the rites of offering daily, has completed the dismissal [of deities], takes a small amount of ash with the thumb and ring finger of the right hand, recites the mantra over it seven times, and then—as previously described—applies it to the crown of the head, the left shoulder, the right shoulder, the heart, below the throat, between the eyebrows, and the hairline to protect the body, they shall be fearless of all things.

If there is anyone who can bathe daily, enter the maṇḍala, and perform this mudrā while reciting the mantra as an offering before the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, that person will cause all the devas, the Māra kings, and the ghosts and spirits to be moved.”

If they hear this mantra, all will give rise to the bodhicitta, becoming compassionate, gentle, and virtuous, never giving birth to evil thoughts; this is due to the majestic spiritual power of these vajras.
It also universally cures all diseases caused by ghosts, causing all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and their assemblies to rejoice greatly.

Furthermore, if a patient has blood coming from the mouth, or if a woman’s menstrual flow does not cease and recurs daily, one should seal raw rice with this mantra, wash it, and take the juice; mixing honey into the juice, one gives it to the woman to drink, and she will be cured immediately after reciting the mantra three times.

10. The Dharma Seal of the Vajragarbha Head (Vajragarbha-śīrṣa-mudrā), the Tenth. Recite the aforementioned Great Mantra: Reverse the two ring fingers so they are within the palms, with the right pressing upon the left; join the palms; extend the two middle fingers and the two little fingers upright so that their tips touch one another; and bend the tips of the two index fingers to press against the nails of the two thumbs.
"This is a single Dharma-seal. If anyone suffers from a headache, they should form this seal and recite the aforementioned mantra while striking their head; the pain will then be cured immediately."

11. The Dharma Seal of the Vajragarbha-Crown (Vajragarbha-śīrṣa-dharmamudrā), Number Eleven. Recite the aforementioned Great Mantra. Following the previous head-seal (*śīrṣamudrā*), modify it only by joining the two index fingers and pressing them against the third phalanges on the backs of the two middle fingers.

"This is a single Dharma-seal. If a person wishes to travel a long distance on foot, they should first perform this seal within their private chamber, recite the aforementioned Great Mantra twenty-one times, and then rub their own soles with this seal; thereafter, the traveler’s feet will not ache."
If one travels on horseback, one should likewise perform the aforementioned mudrā and touch the horse’s legs; thereafter, the traveler’s horse legs will not ache.

Furthermore, when intending to eat while on the road or in any place, first fill a bowl with pure water and add a small amount of food. Stir the water and recite the mantra, then offer it to ghosts and all sentient beings so that they are all fully satiated. If one repeatedly recites the mantra before departing, one will have no fear of dangers from thieves, wild beasts, or other perils encountered on water, land, or along the roads.

12. The Dharma Seal of the Vajragarbha’s Mouth, the Twelfth. Recite the Great Mantra as before. Following the previous Crown Seal (*uṣṇīṣamudrā*), modify it only by having the two ring fingers emerge from the mouths of the two tigers; the two thumbs are both slightly bent at their tips; and the two index fingers are separated from one another, not touching the tips of the thumbs.

"Having formed this mudrā, stand up; with the tips of the toes of the left foot pointing forward and the tips of the toes of the right foot pointing to the right, stand with the body tilted like the Chinese letter 'Ting'."

Then, raise this mudrā to the right of the breast, ensuring it does not touch the breast; face toward the left at an angle, open the mouth wide, and stare with wide-open eyes, manifesting a great expression of wrath like the face of Vajrapāṇi.

"This single Dharma-seal can be used to subdue all celestial Māras and various non-Buddhists; when all powerful ghosts and spirits see it, they will be struck with terror and scatter and perish at once.
It can also cure those afflicted by the illnesses of ghosts and spirits; its efficacy is great."

"If, on the thirteenth day of the tenth month or the fifteenth day of the twelfth month, one adorns a ritual arena within a pure chamber and constructs a water mandala, suspending various banners and canopies."
At the center of the maṇḍala, place a water jar filled with pure water; within it, place the five grains, and seal its mouth with green cypress and bamboo leaves, binding them with a piece of silk.
Thereafter, install an image of Vajrapāṇi and perform the rites of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and self-protection.

Next, set up a brazier and take three types of incense—*kunkuma* (frankincense), *agaru* (aloewood), and *guggulu* (bdellium)—pounding them together to form pellets the size of small jujube fruits, numbering one thousand and eight.

At noon, the mantra-practitioner bathes, puts on fresh, clean garments, enters the maṇḍala, establishes the boundary, and protects himself. He invites the Vajrarāja and installs him within the altar, making various offerings. Within the fire-pit, he draws a flower throne and invites the Vajrarāja to sit upon that flower throne.

Having established the seat, take superior incense pellets and cast them one by one into the fire while reciting a mantra for each. When one thousand and eight pellets have been thus consumed, the Vajra King will manifest upon the Vajra image and ask the practitioner:
"What dharma do you desire?"
At that time, if the practitioner holds the incense burner and answers as they wish, they will immediately obtain great efficacy.

*Vajragarbha-dharṇi-mudrā-mantra*, Chapter Thirteen: "First, with the right hand, press the nails of the little finger, ring finger, and middle finger with the thumb; do the same with the left hand, interlocking them and extending both index fingers upright."
The mantra says:
"Oṃ, ḍa ḍa, ja. This dharma-seal mantra cures all diseases caused by ghosts; its application is highly efficacious.

14. The Vajragarbha Binding Dharma Seal, the Fourteenth. Recite the aforementioned Great Mantra. Following the previous Crown Seal (*mūrdhā-mudrā*), change only this: point the two index fingers behind the middle fingers and twist them together, with the tips touching.

"This is a single Dharma-seal; when treating illness, one should use this seal to bind all ghosts and spirits, reciting the aforementioned Great Mantra, and the demonic afflictions will immediately be cured."

15. The Mantra and Mudrā of the Vajragarbha Arrow Method, Chapter Fifteen: "Interlock the index fingers of both hands by hooking them against one another. Form a fist with the three fingers below the middle finger (the ring, little, and thumb) to create a coil. Press the back of the right wrist over the left wrist. The tips of the two index fingers should be shaped like the notch of an arrow. Kneel upon the ground."
The mantra says:
"Mabakeṇa siddhi dīpa vaṃ vajrapāṇi."

This is the Dharma-seal mantra.

If a person suffers from any illness caused by ghosts, once this seal has been formed, they should kneel on their left knee and place the seal upon the painful area. While the mantra-reciter visualizes in his mind the destruction of the ghost, all [ailments] will be completely cured.

16. The Dharani and Mudrā of the Vajragarbha Spear (Vajragarbhaśakti-dhāraṇī-mudrā) Sixteenth: "Bend the ring finger and little finger of the right hand, pressing the thumb upon the nail. Extend the middle finger and index finger straight upward. Do the same with the left hand. Bend the right arm and place the wrist horizontally across the chest, palm facing downward. Extend the left arm straight toward the left, forming a shape exactly like grasping a spear."
The mantra is:

"Oṃ tīrā-praṇaśani svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If a person suffers from illnesses caused by spirits, ghosts, and the like, they should form this seal; then, rising up and standing on the left foot at an angle in the shape of one grasping a spear, while mentally visualizing the destruction of the ghosts, they should recite the mantra with a sincere mind, and the ghostly illness will be immediately cured.

17. The Vajragarbha-Khadga Dharma Seal. Regarding the Vajragarbha-Khadga Dharma Seal, the seventeenth: recite the aforementioned spear mantra. Following the previous spear seal, the only modification is that the left arm is bent toward the body, held horizontally across the chest with the fingertips pointing toward the right shoulder; the right arm is extended upward, with the wrist standing forward upon the ground.

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If a person suffers from illnesses caused by ghosts or spirits, they should form this seal; the patient will immediately rise and stand with the right foot placed askew, as if striking the child afflicted by the illness, and the ailment will be cured."

18. The Vajragarbha-khaṭvāṅga Seal Mantra. This is the eighteenth Vajragarbha-khaṭvāṅga seal mantra, also known as the Seal for Subjugating All Ghosts. Regarding the mantra, the character *kha* is complete and the character *ṭa* is half-syllabled: "以左右二手後三指俱把捲，以大指押中指節上，頭指直竪" (With the left and right hands, grasp and roll the three rear fingers together; press the thumbs against the joints of the middle fingers; the index fingers are held straight upright).
With the left hand, place the *vajra* seal upright; bend the elbow and turn the palm downward, holding it horizontally across the heart.
With the right hand, extend the side of the hand straight upward, placing it outside the right shoulder.
Rising, he places his left foot to the left and stands with the knee bent.
His right foot remains upright, and he turns his entire body to face the left.
The mantra says:
Namaḥ samantavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpate.
(Namo amu-ratna-dhātāra-ye | Namo śmaśāna-vajrapāṇaye | Mahāyakṣasena-pataye)

"Ju-lam-khyi-liu (12) khu-na (13) svā-hā (14). This is the Dharma-seal mantra.

If a person suffers from a disease caused by malevolent spirits, one should form this seal, assume an expression of wrath, and stand before the patient while reciting the mantra; then all the classes of spirits causing the illness will scatter and flee.

Furthermore, when consecrating the bowl, take a clean copper basin, fill it with pure ashes, and recite the mantra twenty-one times. Then, have a young child bathe thoroughly, dress them in fresh, clean clothes, and have them sit upright upon it.

One should cause both hands to firmly press the rim of the bowl; the mantra-practitioner holds an incense burner in his right hand, burns agallochum incense, and snaps his fingers while reciting the mantra.
In this manner, he should repeatedly recite the mantra and snap his fingers, further rebuking [the obstacle].

"If you wish to apprehend a thief, have the person you suspect sit around the four sides of the bowl. If the bowl comes to rest against his body and does not move further despite further incantations, you should know that this person is the thief.
If it does not come to his body, mark the spot where the thief is sitting with your mind; the bowl will remain wherever it was incanted, and you shall know that this is the thief.
If you do not know the location at all, wherever the bowl eventually comes to rest, know that this is the thief."

Chapter Two: The Chapter on the Dharma-Seals and Mantras of the Vajragarbha Retinue. (In the *Dan* edition, this is not numbered as chapter two. 19. The Dharma-Seal and Mantra of Vajramamaki. (In the *Dan* edition, this is titled "The Vajra Mother" and is numbered first. "Join the two ring fingers and the index fingers, pressing the right over the left and bending them into the palms. Keep the two little fingers side-by-side, straight and upright, with their tips touching. Hold the two thumbs together, standing them upright so that they do not touch the index fingers, and move the thumbs back and forth."
The mantra is:
"Oṃ, kulandari, bandha bandha, svāhā. This dharma-seal mantra is called the Vajramātā Dharma.

If one performs the Vajra rites, or even intends to perform the Vajra rites such as those of Cundā and others, one should first invite this Mother and install her for worship; thus, all Vajras will be delighted, and the practice of the rite will be efficacious.

20. The Mudrā of the Dharma-Standard of Mārīcī. This is the twentieth [chapter], the second in the Dan [edition]. It is not seen in the mantra-text: "Bend the three fingers below the middle fingers of both hands into the palms. Slightly curve and extend the left index finger; extend the right index finger with a greater curve. The tips of these two fingers should be about two finger-widths apart from the thumbs. Extend both thumbs upright side by side."

21. The Seal of Māmakī (Māmakī-gṛhī-mudrā). This is the twenty-first [seal], the third according to the Dan [edition]. It is not seen in the *dhāraṇī*: "The index, middle, and little fingers of both hands are interlaced behind the palms, with the right pressing down on the left; they are bent and held upright. The tips of the two ring fingers touch one another. The two thumbs are crossed outwardly, with the right pressing down on the left, and the wrists are joined."

22. The Dharma Seal and Mantra of Vajramuṣṭi (The Twenty-second [Chapter], also titled the Fourth). Also known as the Vajraputra Dharma, the Messenger Dharma, or the Mātṛka Dharma. "Place the two hands back-to-back, pressing the right forearm against the left forearm. Curl the index, middle, and ring fingers of each hand over the thumbs so that both hands are identical, and cross the two little fingers, pressing them against one another."
The mantra says:
"Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye ||"

If there is anyone who can recite this mantra ten thousand times every day for a full hundred thousand repetitions, they should construct a water-mandala four cubits in size at a place of practice (*dharmapada*).
This mandala shall have no doors; in its center, one should fashion a flower-seat and install the *mudrā* of the Vajra.

Five water jars are placed: one at each of the four corners and one in the center; the openings of all these jars are plugged with cypress leaves and pear branches, which are bound together with three feet of raw silk.
Burn only agalloch incense, light ten oil lamps, and prepare ten platters filled with various kinds of food and drink.
To the west of the altar, near the southern edge on the outside, place a brazier; mix sesame seeds with rice flowers and burn them as an offering.

"Once the mother-siṭṭhi has been seated, the mantra-practitioner shall hold sesame seeds and other substances in his hand; reciting the mantra once for each, he shall cast them into the fire. When this count reaches one thousand and eight times, supernatural efficacy will be attained, and all demonic illnesses shall be completely cured."
If the illness does not subside, perform the ritual for three days; on the third night, bind three grass talismans, inserting many pine torches within them, and perform the Great Dharma.
When all these various rites have been completed, lead the patient to a spacious place and sit facing west.

The mantra-practitioner takes the grass and uses it to kindle a fire; he must recite the mantra with great urgency, without letting the sound cease. Holding the fire, he circumambulates the patient three times to the right, causing the patient to lift his head and gaze at the mantra-practitioner.

The mantra-practitioner holds fire in both hands and, with a wrathful expression on his face, recites the mantra with a sincere mind. After passing a torch made of grass over the patient's head, he continues to hold the fire and hands it to the practitioner; the practitioner takes it and, as before, circles around and passes it over.
Once the three types of grass have been exhausted, his illness will certainly be cured at that moment, and he shall be provided with protection for his person.
"If it is an illness caused by ghosts or spirits, there is none that will not be cured;
if it is not cured, then it must be the result of karmic retribution."

24. Furthermore, the Heart Dharma Mantra of Śaṅkara; [Section] Twenty-Fourth (in the Dan edition, the sixth). Using the aforementioned mudrā, the mantra says:

“Oṃ vajravajriṇi bhagavati vajraśaṅkari he paṇḍapaṇḍa saṃghāṭaya vadratarādite svāhā. This is a single dharma-mantra. If a person wishes to perform the śaṅkāra rite or to treat illnesses, they should daily make offerings, burning agallochum incense and placing cakes, fruits, and various dishes upon platters. At night, having lit lamps within the maṇḍala, they should form the body-seal (kāyamudrā) and recite this mantra with a sincere mind for one million times; then the rite will be accomplished.

"Later, when you merely wish to employ it, if you raise your mind to form the mudrā and recite the mantra, [the deity] will come immediately; if you do not command them to depart, they will never leave.
If you wish to dismiss them, you must recite this mantra to send them away; then you will know that it possesses great efficacy."

25. The Dharani of the Samadhi-Seal of the Small Heart of Śāṅkara, Number Twenty-Five (in the Dan edition, Number Seven). "Turn the four fingers of the right hand upward, bend them so they are closely joined, and place the thumb near the index finger so that they touch one another, just as a vessel filled with water does not leak."

The mantra is: "Oṃ cchambhara-saṅkari hana hana paṇḍa paṇḍa kṣuṇa kṣuṇa hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If someone suddenly contracts a demonic illness and does not know where they feel well or ill, or where they experience pain or itching, one should fill a seal with water, recite the mantra seven times, and then strike the patient’s face and chest with it while saying "phaṭ. All painful areas will be cured, the person will immediately recover their breath, and will return to their former state; this has great efficacy.

26. The *Sāṃkāra-dharmakāya-mudrā*, the twenty-sixth [fascicle], the eighth according to the Dan edition. Recite the previously mentioned *Xiǎoxīnzhòu* (Minor Heart Mantra): "Interlace the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands, with the right pressing over the left within the palms. Stand the two thumbs side by side. Then, bend the middle joints of the two index fingers so that their tips touch, using them to press down on the tips of the two thumbs. Join the wrists and move the thumbs back and forth."

"This is the Single Dharma Seal. If a person wishes to perform the Śaṅkara rite, they must first form this seal and recite the previously mentioned Minor Heart Mantra, using the seal to protect their body; only then may they perform other rites, for which they will be fearless and shall obtain all efficacious results."

27. The Dharma Seal of Śaṅkaradhara, the Twenty-seventh [Chapter], Part Nine of the Old Translation. From this point onward, for all five seals, one recites the previously mentioned Great Heart Mantra.

When constructing the mandala, recite the subsequent Great Dharani; it is efficacious. Following the previous hand-seal (mudrā), the only modification is that the tips of the two index fingers are changed: the right presses down upon the left, placed sideways atop the left thumb, with the wrists joined.

"This is a single Dharma-seal. If there is anyone suffering from a headache, one should form this Dharma-seal and seal the site of the pain, reciting the mantra repeatedly; thereafter, one strikes it with a willow branch, and the illness will immediately be cured."

28. The Mudrā of the Śaṅkara-Śṛṅkhala (The Chain of Śaṅkara). [Tang version: Twenty-eighth; Dan version: Tenth. Following the previous body-mudrā, the only modification is that each index finger is bent so that the backs of the nails touch, and these are placed upon the backs of the two thumbs; then join the wrists.

"This is a single Dharma-seal. If there is anyone possessed by ghosts or spirits, should they form this Dharma-seal and recite the mantra, it will bind all ghosts and spirits, and their illness shall be immediately cured."

29. The Seal for the Method of Healing Illness by Śaṅkara, Part Two of Eleven (in the original text). "Following the previous body-seal, the only modification is that one bends the two tips of the thumbs so that they touch each other, and then places the two thumbs side-by-side, pressing down upon the outer sides of the two index fingers, with the wrists joined."

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If there is anyone afflicted by any demonic illness, they should immediately form this seal and recite the mantra to treat it; that illness will be swiftly cured."

30. The Mudrā of the *Sankarṣaṇa* Method for Subjugating All Ghosts, the Thirtieth [Chapter], the Twelfth in the Revised Edition. Following the previous body-mudrā, the only modification is to extend the two middle fingers so that their tips touch, with the two thumbs held upright side by side. Each of the two index fingers is bent at the middle joint, their tips pressed together to press down upon the heads of the thumbs, while the wrists are joined.

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If there is anyone suffering from piercing pain in the heart or abdomen, they should with a sincere mind fix their mindfulness upon this Seal and seal the site of the pain; by reciting the mantra with single-minded focus, all ghosts and spirits will die, and the illness will be cured."

31. The Dharma Seal of the Great Boundary-Mark of Śaṅkara. [The third and final section; in the Dan version, it is the thirteenth. "Following the previous body-seal, the only modification is to open the index fingers, slightly bending and extending them upward so that they resemble the shape of a cow's horn."

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If one constructs a mandala and performs offerings to treat illness, they should form this seal with their hands and retreat from the western gate of the mandala. Then, embracing the left knee with this seal, they should walk around the mandala on one foot; upon reaching a corner, they turn once, and do so at all four corners."

Next, enter the center of the maṇḍala and form a mudrā by joining the index fingers together; seal the center of the maṇḍala and recite the *Svalpamantra* seven times. Thereafter, perform the *Cundī* rite, which brings freedom from all fear.

32. The Dharma Seal of the Śaṅkara Pāśa (The Thirty-second [or fourteenth according to the Dan edition] Dharma Seal of the Śaṅkara Pāśa). Recite the previously mentioned *Sūkṣma-hṛdaya-mantra*. "May it be so! (Svāhā)"—this is the one hundred and thirty-second phrase. "If one employs these five seals (*mudrā*) and performs the ritual procedures for upholding this Great Dharma Mantra, one will immediately achieve success.

If practitioners who maintain the precepts can give rise to compassion, pity all beings, and extensively provide protection, they may establish a *maṇḍala*, bathe daily, don fresh and clean garments, and before the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas make a great vow:
'May I deliver all sentient beings and be able to eradicate my own suffering and afflictions.'"

Having finished this petition, one should burn agalloch incense and present various offerings of flowers, water, cakes, fruits, and oil lamps. With a sincere heart, one should recite this great mantra for seven days and seven nights, while repeatedly performing the five seals mentioned previously at regular intervals and engaging in repentance.
After the days have elapsed, one should record the number of recitations; it is essential that the count reaches one hundred thousand times, using the counting beads as a marker.

Once the number of recitations is complete, one should then prepare the ritual altar for receiving the Dharma on a chosen day. After completing the offerings and the ritual procedures, one will subsequently obtain various efficacious results.
“The *Śaṅkarā-dharmamaṇḍala*:
‘If a person desires to obtain the miraculous efficacy (*pratyaya*) of Vajra-Śaṅkara, they should first perform various offerings every day and burn agallochum incense.’”

Once you have requested Śāṅkara to arrange the seating, you should recite the heart-mantra one hundred thousand times and make a vow to rescue and protect all sentient beings. Thereafter, seek out a pure location in advance and establish a *maṇḍala* exactly according to the aforementioned ritual.

As for the ritual method: one should select the fifteenth day of the month, bathe with fragrant water, and don new, clean garments. Then, at the site of practice, having fully prepared and suspended various banners, canopies, and offerings such as flowers and incense; once all is complete—
Within that place of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), construct a four-cubit altar using the three colors white, red, and black.
At the center of the altar, place an image of Saṃkāra;
if no image is available, one may instead fashion a mudrā to invoke Saṃkāra and seat him upon a lotus throne, which is also permissible for installation.
Alternatively, it may also be drawn upon the ground.
Draw the form of a vajra in the east, the form of an iron chain in the north, and the form of the khatvāṅga seal in the south.
"As for the form of that mudrā: draw it in the shape of a human face.
On the head of that face, draw a *vajra* symbol standing upright upon it.

Do not depict the body; in place of the body, draw the shape of a staff, with the aforementioned face placed at the top of that staff, making the form of the staff like the shaft of a mendicant’s staff (*khakkhara*)."
On the head of its face, hair is depicted, hanging down in loose strands.
On the right ear, a golden earring is painted, shaped like the fire-god (Agni) in the *maṇḍala* ritual; on the face, it wears a golden earring resembling a small hourglass drum (*ḍamaru*).

"Place the seat of the mantra-reciter in the western direction; upon that altar, arrange eight plates of food, filled with various kinds of superior delicacies, along with twelve lamps and nine water jars."
Each jar was filled separately with pure water, its mouth sealed with green cypress leaves, pear branches, and bamboo leaves, and each branch was tied with three feet of fresh silk cloth.
At the center of the maṇḍala, place one water jar; at each of the four gates and the four corners, place one jar each.

To the south of the western gate of the maṇḍala, set up a fire pit. Use *pārijātaka* wood—two or three bundles of what the Tang call *gǔmù* (grain-wood)—and mix sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, clarified butter (*sarpis*), and honey. Recite the aforementioned heart-mantra one hundred and eight times over them. Likewise, recite this mantra one hundred and eight times over *agallochum* incense (*guggulu*) for the purpose of burning as an offering.

When all preparations have been made, on the fifteenth day of the month, the mantra-practitioner shall again bathe with fragrant water, don new and clean garments, enter the maṇḍala, perform the mudrās for self-protection and the boundary-binding, complete the incense-burning and the ritual of making vows, and then, forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra, invite the Vajra Śaṅkara to be installed, immediately making offerings of various kinds of incense and flowers.

Having completed the offerings, he further invited Śaṅkara to sit within the fire-pit; the mantra-practitioner visualized that within the fire-pit there was a great lotus flower, upon which Śaṅkara’s body sat.

Having formed this thought, take the previously consecrated sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, ghee, honey, and food, etc., and kindle *pārijātaka* wood in the fire pit. Taking small portions of the previously mixed sesame seeds and other substances, recite the mantra once and burn each portion; thus perform one hundred and eight such burnt offerings with mantras.
Furthermore, consecrate the *guggulu* incense, reciting the mantra once for each burning; thus burn it for a full one hundred and eight times.
Finally, burn the ghee and honey, reciting the mantra once for each burning, for one hundred and eight times.
Having thus completed the offerings of incense, flowers, scented water, and various kinds of food and drink,
one should prepare a water altar at a spot about three or four paces to the west of the site of the main mandala.
Upon that altar, place a small couch and have the person receiving the dharma sit upon it; then, holding a water jar, pour the water over their crown.
Command the person receiving the dharma to make this vow with both heart and mouth:
"May my disciple [Name] practice the Śaṅkara-vajra dharma to rescue and protect all classes of sentient beings. May all the Vajras grant my disciple [Name] various signs of spiritual attainment."

Having made this vow, he immediately bestowed the protection upon him; having donned new, clean garments and entered the *maṇḍala*, he performed three prostrations to the Buddha. After further bestowing the protection and forming the mudrā, and having finished reciting the mantra and dispatching [the deity], from that time forward, all various applications thereof attained efficacious results.
"If one wishes to treat illness, it possesses such power that it is like a fierce fire burning dry grass or hot water melting snow.

If a mantra-master wishes to cure a disease, they should construct a water mandala two cubits in size beside the patient. They should recite mantras over white mustard seeds and scatter them in the ten directions to establish a boundary. At the center of the mandala, they should place a plate of cake, a bowl of rice, and a bowl of pure water."
The patient stands by the western gate of the mandala and sits facing east.

The mantra-practitioner holds white mustard seeds in his hand and recites the mantra twenty-one times, striking the patient’s head with them. Thereafter, he burns the white mustard seeds while reciting the mantra another twenty-one times; then, further reciting the Great Mantra, he strikes the patient with a willow branch, and the illness is immediately cured.

If the illness does not subside after one day, perform the rite for three days; it will certainly be cured. From this point onward is the *Aṅkuśī* rite. **34. The Rite of the Vajra-Aṅkuśī Body-Seal Mantra (The Thirty-fourth;

in the Dunhuang edition, the Sixteenth), titled "The Method of the Minor Maiden Vajragarbha."** This contains seven seals and only two mantras: "Interlace the two ring fingers and the two little fingers, placing them within the palms. Straighten the two middle fingers so that their tips touch one another. Hook the two index fingers behind the two middle fingers, aligning their tips beneath the third phalanges so they touch. Join the two thumbs together, each resting upon its respective middle finger. Lock the wrists and move the thumbs back and forth."
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye | Mahāyakṣasenāpate | Oṃ | Vajra-aṅkuśi | ākarṣaya | vikarṣaya | ākarṣayā | vajrāṅkuśini | Svāhā. This dharma-seal mantra is named the Dharma-body Seal Mantra of the Little Daughter of Vajrapāṇi.

If a person wishes to perform rites and offerings for Aṅkuśī, they should first protect their body and establish the boundary by reciting the mantra while forming this mudrā. Then, forming this mudrā once more and reciting this mantra, they should invite Aṅkuśī to be seated and present various offerings; thus, they will immediately cause all Vajras to rejoice.

35. The *Mudrā* of the *Aṅkuśī-mukha-dharma*. This is the thirty-fifth [mudrā], corresponding to the seventeenth in the Dan edition. After reciting the Great Mantra, perform it as follows: "Insert the left and right little fingers straight upward between the two hands; hook the right ring finger over the back of the left ring finger and middle finger, and then insert it into the space between the tips of the left index and middle fingers."
Furthermore, with the left ring finger, pass it through the space between the right middle and ring fingers, then insert it between the right index and middle fingers.
The two middle fingers are held upright, their tips touching one another.
Bend both index fingers to hook the tips of the ring fingers;
hold both thumbs upright and side by side with their tips touching, leaving a space of about half an inch between them and the two little fingers.
"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma, which subdues all the speech of ghosts and spirits, their false words, and their flattery and crookedness.
Once this seal has been formed, recite the subsequent Great Mantra; they will dare not speak again, and the divine illness will immediately be cured."

36. The Dharma Seal of Aṅkuśa (The Elephant Goad). This is the thirty-sixth [seal], also known as the "Seal for Urgently Binding Ghosts" (the eighteenth in the *Dan* edition). [Method: Hold both little fingers upright with their tips touching. Cross the two ring fingers behind the palms, with the right over the left, their tips emerging from the tiger-mouth (the base of the thumb). Hold both middle fingers upright with their tips touching. Hook the two index fingers over the backs of the middle fingers, pressing their tips against the third phalanges. Hold both thumbs upright and join the wrists.

"This is a Dharma-seal. If there is anyone with an illness, they should apply this seal to the location of their pain and recite the great mantra that follows; by sealing the painful area with it, the disease will be immediately cured."

37. The Dhyāna-mudrā of Aṅkuśī (The Hook of Aṅkuśī), the thirty-seventh [or nineteenth according to the Dunhuang manuscript]. Recite the preceding Heart-mantra: "Bend the two little fingers of both hands inward into the palms; press their nails with the thumbs; extend the middle fingers straight; slightly bend the tips of the index fingers and place them against the sides of the middle fingers; raise the arms to the level between the eyes and ears; hold the fingertips horizontally facing forward, but do not let them touch the face."

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If there are spirits or deities who are difficult to subdue or bring under control, and who do not respond to being summoned, one should stand upon the ground and form this seal, reciting the aforementioned Heart Mantra seven times while summoning them; they shall arrive at once in response to the sound."
Once they have arrived, you may at your discretion employ other methods of instruction to subdue them; only after the matter is clearly resolved should you dismiss them.
"The practitioner who upholds this Dharma must understand this, for these dharma-seals and mantras are of the utmost importance to the master."

38. The Dharma Seal of Aṅkuśī (The Hook). This is the thirty-eighth [or, according to the Dan edition, the twentieth] seal. After reciting the Great Mantra, perform the following: Place the palms of both hands back-to-back. Interlace the two ring fingers and extend them like a cord; do the same with the two middle fingers. Bend the two little fingers inward like hooks. Then, bend the two thumbs and further bend the two index fingers, each hooking over the top of the two thumbs, forming the shape of a hook.

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If there are spirits or deities whose minds give rise to opposition and who do not comply with the Buddha-dharma, one should first use the aforementioned Hook Seal to summon them."

Once they have arrived, one should immediately perform this seal-method (*mudrā-vidhi*) and recite the subsequent Great Mantra to bind them and interrogate them; thus all spirits and deities will submit and dare not act with violence—this method is of great efficacy.

39. The Seal of Aṅkuśī’s Mouth (Aṅkuśīmukhamudrā). This is the thirty-ninth [in the main sequence], the twenty-first in the *Dan* edition, also known as the Seal of Liberation. To form it: insert both little fingers inside [the palms] and extend them straight upward; press the right ring finger against the back of the left ring finger and middle finger, and insert [the thumb] between the index and middle fingers.
The left ring finger emerges from between the right middle and ring fingers, then enters the space between the index and middle fingers.
The two middle fingers are held upright, their tips touching one another.
Bend both index fingers to hook the tips of the ring fingers.

Align both thumbs, holding them upright with their tips touching, leaving a space of about half an inch from the little fingers. This mudrā is no different from the previously described "Mouth Mudrā of Amoghapāśa."
"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma (Ekadharmamudrā). If one wishes to liberate the ghosts previously bound, one should release them using the aforementioned heart-mantra.

[Chapter] 40: The Great Dhāraṇī of the Healing Seal of Aṅkuśī; the Forty-second [in the original sequence], also named the Ghost-Binding Seal. Recite the following great dhāraṇī: 'In accordance with the previous body-seal, change only the two index fingers, placing each at the front of the second joint of the middle finger as described in the preceding text. Furthermore, bend both thumbs so that their tips enter the palms, and join the wrists.'"

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If one wishes to subdue all spirits and ghosts, or to treat all illnesses, one should form this seal and press it upon the afflicted area; by reciting the following Great Mantra seven times, the ailment will immediately be cured."
"The Aṅkuśī Great Spell. The spell says: 'Namaḥ ratnatrayāya.'"

This great dhāraṇī-mantra is exceptionally fierce and powerful;
it should not be recited hastily, yet its efficacy in curing illnesses is supreme.

"If there be anyone capable of receiving and upholding this, they must purify their body, maintain the practice of the precepts, remain free from defilement and attachment, and distance themselves from worldly affairs, all impurities, and every form of discursive thought."

If one can protect and uphold [this] in such a manner, the practitioner should bathe daily with fragrant water, put on new and clean garments, enter the maṇḍala, burn agallochum incense and various other substances, provide offerings of food and drink, perform boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and self-protection, and recite this mantra for seven days and seven nights until it reaches one hundred thousand recitations. Only after this is completed should one further enter the Vajra-reception Dharma-maṇḍala.

"Later, when treating illness through the application of this method, one should establish a water mandala, burn agalloch incense, and make offerings of food and drink in whatever quantity is appropriate. Having done so, by forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra, the illness will be cured."

"If the mantra-practitioner approaches the side of the patient possessed by a spirit, and the spirit flees upon his arrival, the practitioner shall immediately stand firm, perform the aforementioned Aṅkuśa-body mudrā, summon the spirit to draw near for treatment, and the illness will be cured."
"The Vajragarbha Anupravicāra Dharmamudrā-mantra has eleven mudrās and four mantras. 41.

The Vajracittānupraviṣṭa-kāya-dharmamudrā-mantra, Number Forty-one (in the Danzhu edition, Number Twenty-three): 'Raise the right hand; from the middle finger downward, extend the three fingers straight upward, keeping them closely joined. Bend the upper joint of the index finger and press it against the upper joint of the middle finger. Furthermore, bend the thumb to press upon the lower joint of the middle finger, while moving the index finger back and forth.'"
The mantra is:

"Oṃ kili kili vajramāraye kīlīlaye svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one wishes to invoke the Great Rite of the随心金剛 (Sui-xin Jingang / Vajra according to One's Heart), one should first perform this seal and recite this mantra to invite him to sit and receive offerings; thus, all Vajras will be pleased, and subsequently, all rites performed will be efficacious.

42. The Vajra-Heart Mudrā for Casting Out Ghosts (Vajracittānuvartana-bhūta-prakṣepa-mudrā). This is the forty-second [mudrā], also known as the twenty-fourth according to the Dan edition. Recite the previously mentioned *Sūkṣma-hṛdaya-mantra* while joining the ring finger and thumb of the left hand together; cast the hand upward, and this constitutes the Casting Mudrā (*Prakṣepa-mudrā*).

43. The Dharma Seal of the Vajra-Heart-Cakra (Vajracittacakramudrā). [Section] Forty-three (in the Dan edition, twenty-five). Recite the previously mentioned *sūkṣma-mantra*: "Flatten the right palm and stroke it downward over the patient's head; this immediately constitutes the Cakra Seal."

44. The Vajra-Anucara-Sakti-Dhāraṇī-Mudrā (The Forty-fourth; in the Dunhuang edition, the Twenty-sixth). Recite the previously mentioned *sūkṣma-hṛdaya-mantra* [while forming the mudrā]: "With the right hand, extend the little finger straight upward; bend the remaining three fingers toward the palm, and press them down with the thumb."

45. The Mudrā for Subduing Māras According to the Heart of Vajra. [Tang version: 27th] Recite the aforementioned *Sūkṣma-hṛdaya-mantra*: "Place the right hand over the back of the left hand; then, extend the right index finger beneath the left little finger and the left index finger above the right little finger, so that all fingers are interlaced vertically."

"Recite the previously mentioned *Suxiao* (Minor Heart) Mantra for these four Dharma Seals; they are all capable of subduing all māras, all great poisons, and malevolent spirits and ghosts, and can likewise shatter hundreds of thousands of millions of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pestilence-bringing demons, as well as all non-Buddhists and raudrākṣas, causing them all to retreat and disperse."
"If there is one who is ill, by performing the ritual with the mudrā and reciting the mantra, the illness shall be immediately cured. **46. The Fourth and Sixtieth [Method]:

The Mudrā and Mantra for Binding Ghosts According to the Vajra-Heart (Vajracittānuvartana-bhūtavidhvaṃsana-mudrā-mantra).** [In the Dan edition, this is the twenty-eighth. "Interlace the two ring fingers of the left and right hands inwardly, with the right hand pressing upon the left. Straighten the two middle fingers so that their tips touch. Hook the two index fingers over the backs of the middle fingers so that their tips meet. Place the two thumbs against the lower joints of the two middle fingers."
The mantra is:
"Oṃ vajradanti dhāraṇīcaryatā śvettihulu hulu maṇtrabhāṭa svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra; if there is anyone who is ill, one should employ this seal and recite the mantra.

Having bound the ghosts, one next recites the mantra over white mustard seeds, burning one seed with each recitation. When this is done one hundred and eight times, all spirits and ghosts will completely retreat and disperse; none shall remain, and the illness will immediately be cured.

47. The Mantra of the Great Dharma-Body Seal of the Vajra-Anucara, Part Fourteen (Tang: Twenty-Ninth). First, grasp the back of the left elbow with the right hand, and then grasp the back of the right elbow with the left hand. Having done so, stand up and raise the seal, placing it upon the head without letting it touch the head. Keep the feet together with toes aligned, and hold the body upright.
The mantra says:
"Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye ||"

This Great Dhāraṇī of the Dharma Seal is able to subdue all—

"If anyone wishes to receive and uphold this mantra, they should proceed before a stūpa containing relics and make offerings of fine incense and flowers to the Vajra. Their practice will then be perfected, and all that they seek shall be swiftly and successfully fulfilled."

48. The Great Dharma Body Seal for Subduing All Unconquerable Ghost Diseases by Following the Mind of Vajra. The Forty-eighth [Chapter]: The Great Dharma Body Seal for Subduing All Unconquerable Ghost Diseases by Following the Mind of Vajra. Recite the aforementioned Great Mantra: "First, with both hands, bend the four fingers below the index fingers and curl them into the palms. Then, erect the two thumbs. Standing up, raise the right hand seal and point it toward the top of the head; strike downward with the force of all ghosts. Cover with the left arm, placing it directly over the heart, but do not let it touch the heart."
Furthermore, extend the left leg straight and then angle it; bend the right knee so that it extends beyond the body and thrust it toward the right; face to the left and stare with both eyes.

"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma. If one performs this single dharma to subdue and eliminate all great flying māras among the devas, rākṣasas, spirits, and ghosts—whether they dwell above, below, or in the four cardinal directions—all shall be extinguished, and none will be able to create obstacles."
"When performing this rite for healing illness, the sound of the mantra must not cease, and one should maintain an expression of wrath; then all will be efficacious. 49. The Fourth Ninth [Method]:

The Body-Seal of the Great Wrathful Vajra Boundary-Binding Rite (The Thirty-First in the Dan Version). Recite the aforementioned Great Mantra: "First, interlace the three fingers from the middle finger downward of both left and right hands with the palms facing outward, pressing the fingers against the backs of the hands. Straighten the two index fingers and bend the two thumbs. Having tensed them so they do not touch the index fingers, stand up and raise the seal toward the right shoulder while angling the left foot forward. Bend the right knee slightly until it nearly touches the body, and turn to the right to assume a face of great wrath."
"This is the Seal of the Great Dharmakāya, named the Dharma of Great Wrath.

If it is used to bind the boundary of the maṇḍala and protect that place, all the various spirits, ghosts, celestial Māras, and their hosts shall fall prostrate to the ground, each scattering and fleeing beyond the borders of the realm."

50. The Vajra-anuvartana-mahākrodha-dharmakāya-mudrā (The Fiftieth [or Thirty-second according to the *Dan* edition], The Great Wrathful Dharmakāya Mudrā of the Vajra-anuvartana). Recite the aforementioned great mantra: "First, with the left and right hands, interlace the three fingers from the middle finger downward so that they all face outward, causing the fingers to rest against the backs of the hands. Then, interlace the two index fingers facing inward, with the right pressing upon the left, and place both thumbs side-by-side, each resting upon its respective index finger. Having done this, stand up and raise the mudrā over the right shoulder. Lean the left foot forward, bend the knee of the right leg, lean the body toward the right, turn the face to look to the left, and glare with wrathful eyes."
"This is the Seal of the Great Dharmakāya; it is fully capable of subduing all difficulties posed by evil Māras, ghosts, spirits, and the like, and it is also used for healing diseases.
If one employs this dharma to subdue all ghosts, spirits, and celestial Māras, they will all be bound of their own accord, utterly pacified, and die, their bodies reduced to fine dust."

"These three Dharma-seals (Dharmamudrā) are all recited together with the aforementioned Great Mantra; they may be employed for all various ritual matters and shall all be efficacious. 51. The Secret Name Dharmamudrā Mantra of Vajragarbha, No. 51 (Tang No. 33):

'Place the right hand across the waist, with the four fingers pointing forward and the little finger pointing backward. Bend the left elbow over the left shoulder, then bend the middle and ring fingers into the palm. Next, extend the thumb, index, and little fingers upright. Tilt the head to the left and gaze intently. Then, make a single sound resembling the clicking of the tongue against the inner cheek.'"
Having uttered this single sound, one should walk with broad strides around the altar to the right, reciting the mantra of praise externally.
The mantra is as follows:

“Śrī-jñānavajra-bharaṇadhā (1) mahāvicayaraśa (2) parādhyantatara (3) mahācandravicayaraśa (4) ehe ehi (5) bhagavan (6) śikhin (7). This is the mantra for the praise of the Dharma-seal (*dharmamudrā*). When performing any ritual of the maṇḍala, after all various arrangements have been completed, one should perform this rite; its secret name is “All-Vajra.”

In this rite, one must always produce sound three times and take three wide strides while circumambulating the altar chanting praises; thus, one will cause all the Vajras of the ten directions to arrive simultaneously to assist in accomplishing the rite, and all various practitioners shall surely obtain efficacious results.

52. The Great Malevolent Universal Body Seal of the Vajra-Anuvartana, No. 52 (also known as No. 34 in the Dan edition). "Insert the right little finger into the space between the left little finger and ring finger, entering from the back."
Place the right ring finger inside the palm, extending straight out between the left middle and ring fingers.
Then grasp both thumbs, pressing them side-by-side against the sides of the middle fingers.

"This seal subdues the eight classes [of spirits] and completely binds all ghosts and spirits; it encompasses the eight classes and all great malevolent ghosts, and contains one thousand six hundred seals of the Vajras."

53. The Seal of the Entire Body (Sarvakāyamudrā), the fifty-third [in the original numbering], the thirty-fifth [in the alternate numbering]. Insert the ring finger of the right hand behind the ring finger of the left hand; place the middle and little fingers of the right hand underneath, aligned with the left wrist.

The tips of the right index finger and the left little finger touch one another; the right middle finger and the left index finger hook together, as do the right little finger and the left index finger.
Insert the left thumb between the right little finger and ring finger; press the back of the second joint of the left index finger with the right thumb.
"This mudrā binds all ghosts in general and also encompasses six hundred minor mudrās."

54. Body Seal (Kāyamudrā), the Fifty-Fourth [in the original numbering], the Thirty-Sixth [in the Dan edition]. Insert the middle finger of the right hand into the back of the ring finger of the left hand, extending it out horizontally across the left wrist. Rest the index finger of the right hand upon the little finger of the left hand, and rest the thumb of the right hand upon the index finger of the left hand. Direct the ring finger and little finger of the right hand toward the palm of the left hand and extend them past the left thumb, emerging from the outer side of the palm.
"This seal subsumes eight hundred minor seals; this seal is also used to bind all ghosts.

(55) Furthermore, the Seal for Summoning According to One’s Heart [Fifth-Fifty] (in the *Dan* edition, the thirty-seventh): Press the palm of the right hand against the back of the left hand, interlace them facing downward, and move the five fingers of the left hand back and forth."

56. The Staff Seal (Daṇḍamudrā), the fifty-sixth [in the Chinese numbering], the thirty-eighth [in the Tibetan numbering]. Reverse the two little fingers, placing them within the palms; interlace the ring fingers and index fingers, with the right pressing upon the left; join the wrists; place the two thumbs side by side, pressing down upon the tops of the two index fingers.

57. The Seal for Seizing the *Zhù* (Seizing the Pestilence), Number Fifty-Seven; Section Three, Number Thirty-Nine. "The four fingers of the right hand grasp and coil [the object], while the thumb presses down upon it; the left hand is likewise."

With the right hand grasping the spear-aid and the left hand grasping the painful area, these are the six mudrās of the Great Evil Universal Body (Mahāpāpaka-sarvakāya). They were translated on the eighth day of the twelfth month in the eighth year of the Daye era of the Great Sui dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta at the Shanglin Garden in Luoyang; the seal texts differ, yet the seals themselves are identical.

The Vajragarbha Dharma-Assembly Mandala: “If there are śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, sons of good family, or others who single-mindedly love and delight in the merit of this secret dharma-treasury of mine, they should, on the thirteenth day of the tenth month or the fifteenth day of the twelfth month, at a pure location—whether in the open air or within a chamber—thoroughly purify and prepare that ground. This shall be exactly as described above for the rites of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, without any difference.”

"Adorn the site of enlightenment by suspending various banners and canopies; prepare all manner of precious objects, ornaments, and various kinds of flowers and incense, and within the site of enlightenment, construct a square ritual altar of four cubits made of five colors."

"The altar has four corners and four gates; at each [gate] place one new, clean water jar. In the center of the altar, construct a lotus seat, and in that center of the altar also place one jar. Beside the fire pit, there is likewise one water jar."
Each of the five jars should be filled to the brim with pure water and provided with the five grains.
The mouths of the jars should each be sealed with cypress leaves and pear branches, and three feet of raw silk should be tied over each; then, one should welcome the image of Vajrapāṇi.
"After placing the water jar in the center, if there is no painted image, one may instead invite Vajrapāṇi through the performance of mudrās; this shall also be faultless.

One should then sequentially arrange forty-nine lamps and place various kinds of food within fifty plates. Furthermore, take these three types of incense—turushka, agallochum, and guggulu—and grind them together to form pills the size of small jujubes, totaling one thousand and eight. Also burn sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, clarified butter, honey, milk, and curd."
"To the south of the western gate of the maṇḍala, place a fire pit. This pit should be constructed by excavating into the ground, measuring one cubit on each of its four sides and one cubit in depth.
Within the fire pit, draw a lotus flower."
“Having prepared all the various requisites, bathed in fragrant water, and donned fresh, clean robes, enter the maṇḍala and perform the mudrās to protect the body.
Once the boundary has been established, perform the mudrās to summon the Vajra Bodhisattvas and seat them in their places.”

First, perform the ritual of offering flowers and incense; next, perform the offerings of various dharmamudrās and mantras; then, burn sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, ghee, and honey mixed together as an offering, exactly according to the method described above.

Thereafter, take the previously prepared incense pellets and, having recited the Great Heart Mantra over each one individually seven times, cast them into the fire to burn; continue in this manner until one thousand and eight pellets have been completely consumed.
"At that time, the body of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbharāja will manifest upon the vajra image and ask the practitioner:
'What dharma do you desire?'"
At that time, the practitioner shall take up the incense burner and respond according to their wishes.
Once King Vajragarbha has fulfilled their vow, he will suddenly vanish; the practitioner shall immediately receive the sign of accomplishment at that very moment.

"Once the offerings have been completed, take the water jars from within the mandala in succession and exit the maṇḍala. Proceed to the water-altar and, in order, pour the water over the heads of those who have received the Dharma."

Once each has been consecrated, they shall don new, clean garments and be led into the maṇḍala. After they have prostrated before the Buddha, the protection of their bodies shall be performed exactly according to the method described above.
Then, bid farewell to the Bodhisattva Vajragarbharāja, clear the site, and distribute the remaining food to all sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, including Vajragarbha and others, saying:
"You and your retinues have now offered these various mantras, a subtle, profound, and rare treasury of secret dharmas, by which such beneficial matters are obtained."
I too have studied this Dharma since ancient times and have achieved its full realization.

You all must likewise firmly maintain the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*), remaining ever without regression, and attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Return to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha; constantly traverse the six realms of existence to provide protective mindfulness, exhorting others to awaken the Bodhicitta, and do not shrink from toil or weariness.
"Because of the power of your vows, we praise and bring fulfillment to all your joys.
When the great assembly heard the Buddha’s confirmation, they were all filled with great joy; they paid their respects and departed.
