The Chapter on the Seal and Mantra of the Sovereign Spiritual Power of the Bodhisattva Vajramṛtyuvaśaṃkara. There are twenty-one seals and fifteen mantras;

fourteen mantras are primary and one mantra is auxiliary. At that time, the World-Honored One, together with Mṛtyuvaśaṃkara, Ucchuṣma, and others, assembled and proclaimed this Great Sovereign Powerful Dhāraṇī Dharma-Seal Divine Mantra.

At that time, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways. Vināyakas, malevolent spirits, and other non-believers were struck with great terror; they wished to flee into the mountains but could not go, and they wished to enter the sea but could not depart either. Having no place to hide or escape, they ran to the presence of the Buddha, prostrated themselves with their heads touching the ground, and entreated the Buddha for protection.
The Buddha said:
"Stop, stop! You need not fear that the vajra will strike your heads and shatter them into seven pieces.
Have you not heard how King Mahābhiṣaṇa was once struck and crushed to death by the vajra on Mount Sīkhaṇḍa? Do you remember this?"
Because this Vajra of mine possesses great power, if there should be anyone who recites and upholds the dhāraṇīs,

mudrās, and other rites of the Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, and Devas, making daily offerings and extensively performing repentance, or when they wish to rescue and protect all sentient beings from calamities and hardships— at such times, you spirits and deities must all provide protection and assistance, and must not cause them distress or confusion.
If there are those who recollect these dharmas of mantras and mudrās, you must watch over them closely and ensure that no evil spirits or ghosts find an opportunity to disturb or harass them.

Furthermore, if there are those who have inadvertently consumed the flavors of alcohol, meat, or the five pungent roots, or who have mistakenly eaten impure fresh blood, you must likewise endure this and not disturb them.
“If you are able not to disobey my words, I shall cause you all to escape such a perilous and fearful calamity.
At that time, King Gaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! [I shall do as you say.]”

If there are those who recite and uphold the mantras, mudrās, and maṇḍalas of the Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, and devas, and who are constantly able to protect the practice of the essential dharmas of all Buddhas and extensively arrange offerings, we and our retinues, having received the Buddha’s command, shall not allow any malevolent ghosts or spirits to create obstacles.

Furthermore, if there are those who recite and uphold the Buddha’s dhāraṇīs, and perform the mudrās and maṇḍalas, constantly making offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, Prajñāpāramitā, the Bodhisattvas, the Vajras, the devas, and so forth, we shall protect and mind them.

If one causes the mantra-reciter to give rise to various conceptualizations—such as causing them to become ill, causing their vision to darken, or causing them to think of wealth and sensual pleasures—then due to these thoughts and recollections, one will not cause sentient beings to enter the mandala every day to recite the Buddha’s *dhāraṇī* mantras and perform ritual mudrās;
even if they do recite and maintain them, it will be in vain and without efficacy, all because such conceptualizations prevent accomplishment.

Furthermore, if there is someone who, desiring to make offerings by burning incense, scattering flowers, providing food, or preparing various ritual implements, has those items stolen away by ghosts or spirits, causing the practitioner reciting mantras to fail in their ritual performance.
I shall provide protection for all such matters as these.
As for all evil demons, spirits, and their like who pursue people, I shall entirely ward them off and prevent them from following after.

Furthermore, if there are those who recite and uphold the dhāraṇīs and mudrās of my Buddha’s True Dharma, even if they should by mistake commit an offense by eating mixed flavors, or if their food contains various impurities, pungent or strong-smelling herbs, blood vessels, or foul odors; or if they should happen to associate intimately with women—I shall not cause them any hindrance or affliction. This is entirely because I protect those who practice the Dharma.
At that time, Vajragarbha said:

"If there should be anyone who upholds this dhāraṇī, the Dharma-seal of all Buddhas, and who fears being defiled by impurities or apprehends having committed the aforementioned transgressions, they should diligently bathe and frequently proclaim the prohibitions and precepts. Reciting the dhāraṇī seven times every morning at dawn, and likewise at mealtime, they shall immediately shatter all obstacles; in whatever rites they perform, they will be entirely fearless, and everything shall be successfully accomplished."

At that time, when the Bodhisattvas Vajrasena, Cāritra, and others had finished expounding this secret method of skillful means within the assembly of the Buddha, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas unanimously approved and simultaneously praised them, saying:
"Our heart's aspiration is as you have spoken; you all should believe and accept it, pay homage, and respectfully practice it."

**Chapter One: The Dharma-Seal Mantra of the Incense Burner of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha-Kuṇḍali’s Sovereign Spiritual Power** **The First: The Dharma-Seal of the Kuṇḍali Incense Burner** Using the Lesser Heart-Mantra: "Turn the palms of both hands upward. The middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands are extended straight upward with their backs touching one another. The two index fingers are held slantwise and straight, their tips pressed against each other. The two thumbs are extended, resting against the second joints of the index fingers."
The mantra is:

"Oṃ āmiti uṃ phaṭ. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one performs any Vajra ritual, first seal the incense burner with this seal, recite the small-heart mantra twenty-one times, and then burn the incense; all will be delighted.

2. The Mudrā for the *Kuṇḍalī* Perfume Rite. The second [section] on the mudrā for the *Kuṇḍalī* perfume rite employs the "Minor Heart Mantra": "Interlace the five fingers of the right hand, holding them straight and upright toward the front; with the left hand, grasp the underside of the right wrist, facing outward."

"This is the Single Dharma Seal. If, within the sacrificial altar of a Dharma assembly, one places various flowers and powdered incense into a jeweled basin filled with water, and having formed this seal, seals the water with its mantra and places it before the Buddha, all will rejoice."

3. The Mudrā for the *Kuntali* Body-Protection Method. This third [method] employs the Great Heart Mantra: "Interlace the two little fingers within the palms. With the two ring fingers, bend them double and insert them into the palms, pressing them down upon the interlaced little fingers. Join the wrists. Stand the two middle fingers upright with their tips touching. Slightly bend the two index fingers so that they rest behind the joints on the backs of the middle fingers, without touching them."
The mantra is:

"Oṃ (1) hulu hulu (2) tiṣṭha tiṣṭha (3) bandha bandha (4) hana hana (5) amṛte (6) hūṃ phaṭ (7). Recite this mantra seven times; it is the Dharma-seal mantra. If there is anyone who constantly wishes to uphold the Vajra-dharma, at dawn each day, after washing their hands and face, they should take pure water in their right hand, recite the mantra seven times, and then scatter it toward the east. After scattering it three times, they should sprinkle themselves with the remainder, and then enter the room to perform the rite of self-protection.

Regarding the method for protecting the body: having burned incense, one should form the mudrā and not release it, reciting the heart-mantra with the mouth while wearing the mudrā upon the crown of the head. Next, seal the left shoulder; next, the right shoulder; next, the front of the chest; next, below the neck; next, between the eyebrows; next, at the hairline; next, on the crown of the head; and finally, behind the crown. Thus, seal each of these eight locations three times each; this is called the method for protecting the body.

"When any person wishes to perform Vajra rites, they should first seal the incense burner. Having finished burning the incense, holding the incense burner in hand, they should address the Buddhas of the ten directions, Prajñā, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, hidden sages, and the various devas of the paths of karma, exactly according to the aforementioned method."

Having finished the invocation, one should immediately perform this rite and then proceed with its application; one will be entirely fearless, and there shall be no difficulty in performing the ritual or reciting the mantra.
4. The Mantra and Seal for the Rite of *Cundā* to Expel *Vināyakas*. Fourth: "Bend the left thumb across the palm and grasp it with the left middle finger and ring finger."

Furthermore, extend the index and little fingers outward and bend them, so that the tip of the index finger reaches the side of the middle joint of the middle finger, and the tip of the little finger reaches the side of the middle joint of the ring finger.
Then extend the arm and rotate it to the right, reciting the mantra seven times.

While performing the ritual, press the thumb of the right hand against the nail of the little finger, cross the arm behind the waist to the right side, and extend the tips of the three fingers forward.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ hūṃ hanasatnatata vidambhaya ucchādaya huṃ phaṭ phaṭ. This dharma-mudrā mantra is fully capable of warding off and expelling all yakṣas, piśācas, and nāgas.

Whether it be for the Buddha, Prajñā, the Bodhisattva, or Vajra, wherever one intends to perform a ritual assembly, one must first form this mudrā and recite the mantra; then all evils will immediately disperse, all matters will be accomplished, and there will be no fear whatsoever.
It is just as when a king performs his movements and rituals: he must first clear away [obstacles] before acting;
this case is likewise.
"Regarding this mudrā and mantra: if one uses the mudrā within a room, one should circle it three times clockwise around the head while reciting the mantra seven times."

When constructing the altar, perform the "walking with extended arms" ritual, circumambulating the altar three times by walking on the outside; first lift the right foot, then lift the left foot, reciting the mantra twenty-one times, though it is also well to recite it many more times.

5. The Mudrā and Dhāraṇī of the Single-Syllable King-Subduing Vajra Cundā, Fifth. "Interlace the two little fingers within the palms, pressing the right over the left. Cross the two ring fingers behind the middle fingers. Hold the two middle fingers upright with their heads touching side-by-side. Hook the two index fingers around the tips of the two ring fingers. Press the two thumbs against the heads of the two middle fingers so that their tips are level. Rest the heads of the two middle fingers and thumbs upon the crown of the head, and assume a wrathful facial expression."
The mantra is:

"Oṃ, jvala jvala jvala jvala jvala, hūṃ hūṃ, phaṭ. If one constructs a site for any maṇḍala, one should first bind this mudrā and recite the mantra, circumambulating the altar seven times; then all māra kings will universally submit and be subdued.

6. The Mantra for the Mudrā of Establishing the Boundary of the Army of Cundī. Sixth. "First, place the right middle finger so that its tip points toward the back between the left index and middle fingers. Next, do the same with the ring finger between the left little fingers."
Turn the left middle finger inward; place the tips of the right index and middle fingers between them, pointing inward; then do the same with the left ring finger between the right little fingers.
Join the tips of the two little fingers and the tips of the two index fingers; likewise join the tips of the two thumbs with their heads pointing downward.
When performing the rite, join the thumbs with their tips touching the ground and extend the two arms so that the elbows form wings.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ, kili kili, vajrapuṭe, bandha bandha, hūṃ, haḥ. This Dharma-seal mantra is able to eliminate all evil spirits and ghosts within the earth, down to the adamantine limit.

If one is at the site of a Dharma assembly or a ritual mandala, one should form this mudrā and recite the mantra seven times while pressing the mudrā against the ground; this will cause all malevolent spirits, both upon the earth and beneath it, down to the very limit of the vajra-realm, to disperse entirely so that none can inflict harm.

7. The Dharani for the Mudrā of Establishing the Four-Directional Boundary of Cundī. The seventh [section]: "In accordance with the previous earth-mudrā, change only this: extend the two thumbs apart by two inches, point the tips toward the body and hold them upright, then thrust the fingers and rotate them to the right."
The mantra is:
“Oṃ sarā sarā vajra parakāra huṃ phaṭ. This dharma-seal mantra is able to eliminate all evil māras, ghosts, and spirits from the four directions.

If one is at a place where a Dharma assembly or ritual altar is held, one should form this mudrā and recite the mantra seven times; then, using this mudrā, one should face the four directions and turn to the right with the sun, whereby all yakṣas, bhūtas, and other such spirits will completely retreat and disperse.

8. The Mantra and Dharma-Seal for Binding the Realm of Space by Cundī. This eighth [section] is also called "Binding the Boundary Above. Following the previous earth-seal, one only changes the two thumbs, each placing them against the side of the index finger. Then, with this seal directed toward the head, rotate it three times to the right.
The mantra is:

“Oṃ viṣpuraṭa vajra pañjara huṃ phaṭ. This Dharma-seal mantra can eliminate all demons, evil spirits, and ghosts from the void up to the summit of existence; they shall not dare to harbor evil thoughts.

Immediately, with this mudrā raised above the head, rotate it three times to the right and recite the mantra seven times; all yakṣas, bhūtas, and other spirits who fly through the heavens and the void will be completely dispersed.
"In an assembly for the Great Maṇḍala Dharma Altar, one must perform this sealing mantra and binding protection three times or seven times.
First, one should select an auspicious site; even before the layout has been established, this constitutes the first round of boundary-binding and the expulsion of obstructive spirits."

Second, when the ground has been leveled, made even, and rendered firm and solid, and it has been smeared with fragrant mud, one should again perform a single round of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and expulsion (*vidhūnana*) while offering a small portion of famous incense and fine flowers.

Third, having erected the central pillar so that it touches the forehead and having hung the banners, canopies, bells, and pendants around its perimeter, one should again offer a small amount of incense and fine flowers while performing the circumambulation; at that time, one should once more perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) to ward off obstructive spirits.
Fourth, having arranged the colored powders and flower seats and opened the various positions and stages, one again performs a single round of boundary-binding and expulsion.
Fifth, having brought the lamps into the maṇḍala and installed them, one again performs a single round of boundary-binding and expulsion.

Sixth, one should take water jars, flowers, incense, food and drink, ghee, honey, sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, and all other articles of offering, and place them entirely within the maṇḍala; once they have been fully arranged, one should again perform a single recitation of the boundary-binding and expulsion ritual.

Seventh, when one wishes to invite the Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, Devas, and so forth, before the invitation, one should again perform the boundary-binding and expulsion ritual once more; during the interval of binding the boundaries, one should bind each of the great-body dharma-mudrās and hold the *vajra* to protect the boundary.
Having subdued the great hosts of Māras, one performs each of the bodily rites in succession.

Next, holding a censer in the right hand, one circumambulates three times to perform the binding and protection of the boundary (*sīmābandha*). One should mentally designate the offerings, ensuring that all movements and postures are fully endowed with the characteristics of the Dharma (*dharmalakṣaṇa*).

Thereafter, one shall cause all Buddhas, Prajñā, all Bodhisattvas, all Vajras, all vidyādharas, all devas, and all paths of karma to be greatly delighted by the offerings made; then, one by one, each shall form their respective root mudrās, recite their respective root mantras, and perform the invitation and offering.
"This dharma for establishing the boundary (*sīmā-bandha*) is just like the conduct, movements, and majestic deportment of a sovereign king;

there is not the slightest difference between them. **Chapter 9: The Dharma Seal of the Body of Kuntali.** The Dharma Seal of the Body of Kuntali, Chapter Nine. Using the *hsiao-hsin chu* (Minor Heart Mantra): "Interlace the two little fingers within the palms. Hook the two ring fingers together, bending them inward into the palms, and press them down upon the interlaced little fingers. Join the wrists. Stand the two middle fingers upright with their tips touching. Bend the two index fingers to pinch the upper joints of the middle fingers. Align the two thumbs side by side to pinch the middle joints of the middle fingers. Move the index fingers back and forth."

"This is the Single Dharma Seal; if anyone wishes to perform the *kuntaḷī* rite for making offerings or for curing illnesses, they should employ this seal for all purposes, including summoning and sending away [spirits]."

10. The Dharma-Seal for the Incense and Flower Offering to Cundī. This tenth [section] employs the Great Heart Mantra: "Interlace the two ring fingers and the two little fingers, pressing the right over the left within the palms; then bend them toward the wrists. Straighten the middle fingers so their tips touch obliquely, and with each of the two index fingers, pinch the third phalanx of its respective middle finger. Place each of the two thumbs against the side of its respective index finger, and join the wrists."
"This is the Seal of the Single Dharma; wherever one may be, whether at a site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) or a dharma altar, one should perform this seal.
Taking a single flower and a pellet of incense, place them within the seal; having formed this seal, recite the mantra as an offering."
If there are no incense or flowers, one who makes this seal as an offering will cause all Vajras to rejoice.

11. The Seal for the Ritual Offering of Food and Drink to Cundī. Regarding the ritual offering of food and drink to Cundī, the eleventh [section]: employ the Great Heart Mantra. Following the previous seal for incense and flowers, simply change the two little fingers and the two ring fingers so that they are extended within the palms, and open the palms.

"This is the Single Dharma Seal. If one intends to offer food and drink upon the altar, one must seal each individual dish with this seal; after reciting the mantra over each one, one may then enter the altar to arrange them for offering."
If there is no food or drink, simply forming this mudrā as an offering will also cause all the Vajras to rejoice.

12. The Mudrā and Mantra for the *Cundī* Lamp Ritual, Number Twelve. "Place the last two fingers of the right hand bent into the palm. Extend the middle finger straight upward. Bend the index finger toward the palm. Bend the thumb at its middle joint and press it against the upper joint of the index finger; then, with the side of the tip of the thumb, grasp the middle joint of the middle finger."
The mantra is:

“Oṃ virujiṇi svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one is making offerings within the altar or the site of practice (*maṇḍala*), one should apply this seal to each individual lamp, recite the mantra while sealing them, and then set them down.

14. The Mudrā of the *Kuntalī-śikhara-dharma*. This fourteenth [mudrā] employs the Great Heart Mantra. "This is the Seal of the Single Dharma, also known as the Ghost-Binding Seal.

Furthermore, if there is someone suffering from a headache, having formed this mudrā, they should press it upon the painful spot and recite the Great Heart Mantra. Moreover, by consecrating a willow branch with the mantra and striking the painful spot with it, the pain will immediately be cured.

15. The Mantra and Seal of the Kunte-li-tooth Method (Kunte-li-tooth Dharani-mudra), Number Fifteen. Using the Great Heart Mantra, one may also cure illnesses. "With the little finger of the left hand, press against the back of the base of the ring finger; next, bend the middle finger and press it down from behind the ring finger onto the back of the little finger, then bend its upper joint so that it lies flush alongside the ring finger."
Next, bend the middle joint of the index finger and press it against the edge of the small fingernail, with the tip of the finger pointing toward the palm and resting alongside the ring finger.
Next, place the thumb obliquely over the edges of the index and middle fingernails, also resting alongside the ring finger, while the ring finger is held straight and upright.
To eliminate all *vināyakas*, perform this mudrā and mantra seven times, circumambulate three times to the right, and strike with the fist while turning it.
The mantra is:

Alternatively, if one recites the Great Mind Mantra forty-nine times, the pain will be cured instantly; this method is highly efficacious.
"If treating demonic illnesses, at the time of binding the spirit, blood will immediately spurt from the patient's mouth; it cures all diseases."
"If one uses the Tooth Seal (Dantamudrā), reciting the mantra repeatedly while facing a government office, the officials will rejoice and their anxieties will be dispelled.

16. The General Seal of Cundavajrā, the Sixteenth. Using the Great Heart Mantra: 'With the left hand, press the thumb against the nail of the little finger; the remaining middle, index, and ring fingers are all held straight and upright, splayed upward.'"

"This is the Single Dharma Seal; however, for all incense, flowers, lamps, food, drink, and every kind of offering implement prepared for the site of the Dharma assembly altar, each and every one must be marked with this seal."

If a vajra is not available, then one should use this seal to mark all the offering implements—thereby ensuring that all classes of evil ghosts and spirits will not dare to violate or touch them.

"If a woman suffers from constant menstrual flow, or if men or women suffer from blood coming from the nostrils, one should take two *liǎng* each of *rasāñjana* and the root of *manḍūkaparṇī*. There is another method with a similar name: take granulated sugar, saffron flowers, and clarified butter (*ghṛta*), pound them together until they resemble an ointment. If one suffers from nasal congestion, a foul odor within the nose, or an inability to perceive fragrant or foul odors, one should administer this aforementioned medicine as a nasal drop, and one will be cured.

The remaining cases may be understood by analogy. If a person cannot eat, suffers from jaundice, has yellowed eyes, has large gas-bloated masses in the abdomen, is unable to breathe, or suffers great pain in the throat, one should take rock salt, asafoetida, harītakī, cumin seeds, dried ginger, pippalī, and black pepper—these seven ingredients in equal parts, each weighing half a *liang*. 20. The Great Protective Seal of Cundī. This twentieth [seal] is used following the Great Mantra: "Stand up, facing straight forward. "If a messenger is sent from the patient's household to inquire of the master, the master shall form this mudrā and recite the mantra. If, while sleeping, he sees in a dream the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Vajrapāṇis, devas, or others, the illness will be cured;

First, with the right hand, bend the thumb into the palm and clench the remaining four fingers into a fist, pressing it under the left armpit. Next, with the left hand, likewise clench a fist as with the right and press it under the right armpit. "This is the Dharma-body Seal (*dharmakāya-mudrā*). Assuming an expression of great wrath, one should recite the following Great Mantra without ceasing the sound of the chanting. As one performs the circumambulation three times, all [spirits] will disperse and the illness will immediately be cured.

"If used when establishing the boundaries for constructing a ritual altar, it possesses great spiritual efficacy. 22.

With the left hand, cross the "tiger-mouth" (the base of the palm) behind the waist, with the four fingers pointing forward and the index finger pointing backward.
With the right hand, grasp a *vajra*, holding the arm upright and exerting great force—if there is no *vajra*, simply clench the hand into a fist as if grasping a *vajra*-staff.
Assuming a face of great wrath, recite the subsequent Great Mantra. If one extends the thumb, it is called the Axe-Grip Seal (*paraśugraha-mudrā*).

To employ it, use the subsequent great mantra: "Turn the palms upward; interlace the three fingers [of each hand] with the right pressing over the left; hold the two index fingers upright and slightly askew so that their tips touch; and bend the thumbs of each hand to press against the upper joints of the sides of the middle fingers."
Turn the palms outward as if rising; point with the index fingers downward toward the head, placing them level with the eyebrows.

Stand up, planting the right foot firmly on the ground, drawing the left leg back so it aligns exactly with the right knee. With the sole of the foot facing downward in a stamping posture, press the heel against the upper part of the knee. Then, with eyes bulging, assume a look of great wrath, with the head inclined slightly forward.

"This is the Dharmakāya Seal; if one performs it at the site of any maṇḍala rite, having bound this seal, one should walk around the maṇḍala three times with one foot raised. One will be fearless in all respects, and whatever is undertaken shall be accomplished."
"If one performs this seal at the site where a disease is being treated while beside the patient, and recites the subsequent great mantra, that illness will be cured immediately.
If one does not understand this method of walking on one leg in all mandala sites, none of the mandala rites will be accomplished."

"Vajrapāṇi ratnodbhavati svāhā.
This is a great mantra that is fully capable of dispelling all obstacles and difficulties.

"If a person desires to receive and uphold this mantra, they should daily bathe with fragrant water until clean, put on fresh and pure garments, and after protecting their own body, enter the *maṇḍala* site to construct a water altar—four cubits in length and breadth, with the methods for adorning the altar as described in other sections. Once the adornment is complete, they shall immediately perform the ritual of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*)."
In the center of the mandala, place the seat of the Vajra Cundī; if there is an image of her, invite it and install it there;
if there is no image, one may visualize her in the mind, form the mudrā, and likewise invite her to sit.

Scatter various kinds of flowers and burn agalloch incense; after reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times repeatedly, construct a five-colored mandala in a pure place, adorned as previously described in other sections.

Entering into this *dāna*, one scatters various flowers, burns various incenses, and makes offerings of various foods, drinks, lamps, and light; one then makes vows and recites mantras, burning ghee, honey, and other substances in the fire pit—offering them either one hundred and eight times or one thousand and eight times—for as long as seven days or two weeks. Once the count is complete, one’s wishes will be fulfilled; thereafter, whatever one does according to one’s heart will succeed. It is highly efficacious for curing illnesses, subduing all evil demons and spirits, and ensuring that wicked humans or non-humans can cause no harm.

26. The Mudrā and Dhāraṇī for Binding the Great Boundary through the Kuṇḍalī Samaya. This is the twenty-sixth [chapter], also known as the *Sarvabuddha-mahāsamaya-mudrā-dhāraṇī*. [Method: Interlace the two little fingers and the two ring fingers, pressing the right over the left, and extend them upward within the palms.
Straighten the two middle fingers, extending them diagonally with their tips touching.
Bend each of the two index fingers to press against the back of the third phalanges of the middle fingers.
Place each of the two thumbs alongside the outer edges of the index fingers and open the palms.
The mantra is:

"Oṃ śaṅkari mahāsamaye paṇḍa paṇḍa svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one establishes a site for the *maṇḍala* altar and wishes to invite all Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, Devas, and others to make offerings, once the holy assembly has arrived, one should individually perform the Flower-Seat Seal-mantra for each to welcome and install them in their respective positions; when this is completed, they are all settled.

Thereafter, perform this dharma-mudrā while reciting the mantra; turning it clockwise three times or seven times is permissible in both cases. This is called "quiet alertness," and it is known as the method of internal and external strict seclusion.
Once these rites have been performed, the assembly of noble ones shall all sit at ease and receive the offerings.

"If the mantra-practitioner does not understand how to perform this rite, many malevolent māras, external spirits, and vināyakas will find an opportunity to cause harm, and thus there will be no peace."

"The treatment of illness is likewise. One should perform various rites of offering; when these general services are completed, one again forms this mudrā and recites the mantra seven more times—reciting only the previous mantra 'Banda banda,' adding 'Vañja vañja' below it, and finally saying 'Svāhā.'"
Rotate the seal counter-clockwise three times, reciting the mantra seven times; this is called "Dissolving" and is also called "Opening the Lock.
If one employs it without following this method, the mantra-practitioner will incur calamity.
"It is like a king who commands his ministers to hold a banquet, dispatching generals and soldiers to guard the streets and ensure that the gates are firmly secured so that no one may enter;
when the event concludes and they are about to disperse, it is just the same."
27. The Dharani of the Seals and Mantras of the Messenger Kumārajīva, Part Two. Twenty-seven. "The seal is the same as the seal of the Prajñā messenger; the thumbs move back and forth."
The mantra is:
“Oṃ, vīru vīru, kārāja kārāja, hana hana, svāhā. This is a single dharma-mantra; if one wishes to have the messenger cure a disease, one should recite this mantra;
if one leaves the messenger behind to go and attend to the patient, one should likewise recite this mantra.
"When treating an illness with the *muñjapila* rite, one shall dispatch a messenger to attend to the patient.
If the *muñjapila* remains, the messenger may depart;
if the *muñjapila* departs, the messenger shall remain."
In this manner, each [rite] possesses its own efficacy.

Regarding the *Muṇḍalī-vajra-dhāraṇī-vidhi-maṇḍala*: "If one wishes to receive and maintain the *Muṇḍalī* rite, one should first paint its image: the entire body is blue, both eyes are red, and the hair is gathered into a topknot."
The color of his hair was a mixture of black and red, like the flames of samādhi.
With eyes wide open in great rage, all his upper teeth were bared as he bit his lower lip, assuming a face of intense wrath.
There were two red snakes with their heads intertwined, hanging from his chest with their heads tilted upward.
The tails of both snakes each passed through the ears of the image, their tips hanging down to his shoulders.
The two snakes are yellowish in color like the *huhu* snake, with red and black markings interspersed.
Their forms each have eight arms; the uppermost right hand holds a *vajra*, with the arm bent upward.

In the second position below, he holds a long halberd with his hand; his arm is bent upward, and the halberd has three prongs at both its upper and lower ends, all of which are sharp-edged, with one end pointing upward and the other end resting upon the ground.
The lower third arm presses against the left third arm, with the two arms crossed over the chest.
In the right hand, he grasps two red snakes whose bodies are intertwined, both facing toward the face of the image; the left hand likewise grasps the head of a single red snake.

Form the *vajra-mudrā* with both hands: press the thumbs against the nails of the little fingers, while extending all other fingers. Then, press the left hand over the front of the right armpit, followed by pressing the right hand over the front of the left armpit; this is the body-seal (*kāya-mudrā*).
The fourth arm below is extended downward, not touching the right hip; all five fingers are straightened, forming the *abhaya-mudrā*.
The upper left hand holds a golden wheel; the arm is bent upward, and the wheel has eight spokes with a complete hub and rim.

In the first hand of the lower position, bend the three fingers below the middle finger toward the palm; the thumb presses against the side of the upper joint of the middle finger; the index finger is held straight upright and extended upward; then bend the elbow, with the forearm directed to the left.
The fourth hand below is held horizontally across the left hip, with the fingertips pointing to the right.

On both wrists are golden bracelets. The ground is purple and strewn with flowers. He wears a celestial robe of brocade draped over his shoulders, neck, and back, with the hems of the robe falling downward on either side of his head. His waist is bound with a belt consisting of green outer fabric and red inner lining. His two hips are covered with tiger skin and brocade.
"On each of his two lower legs there is a red snake coiled around them; the colors of these two snakes are a variegated intermingling of red and black.

Furthermore, the image is made to stand upon a pair of lotus flowers made of the seven treasures; the toes of his right foot point toward the right side, and the toes of his left foot point toward the left side."

"To the left of the image, below the ankle, paint a king of ghosts with a body resembling that of a human, coarse and large in stature, having the head of a white elephant; he sits in a kneeling posture with his knees bent, raising his head upward to gaze up at the face of the image."
That ghost holds the root of a radish in its right hand, with the arm bent upward.
Its left arm is bent flat, with the hand extended and the palm facing upward, holding a *huānxǐtuán* (joy-balls).
Both wrists of that hand are adorned with golden bracelets.
The neck of this spirit is adorned with a golden necklace, its waist is bound with a green sash, and its two cheeks are covered with scarlet brocade.

Once this image has been painted, seek out a pure room—a Buddhist hall will also suffice—and within it, burn incense and offer this invocation: excavate away the foul earth, tiles, stones, dung, and other such refuse; then bring in clean yellow earth from another location to fill the excavated space, tamping it down firmly to make it level, with all four sides perfectly equal.

The mantra-master shall immediately bathe in fragrant water and don fresh, clean robes; the patron shall do likewise, and together they shall establish a ritual arena for repenting karmic obstacles and receiving the Dharma.
"First, smear the site of the practice ground once with fragrant mud. Next, perform the ritual for binding the boundary (*sīmābandha*).

Then, fashion four stakes from *khadira* wood, each measuring eight finger-widths in length; recite the Great Heart Mantra over these stakes one hundred and eight times and drive them into the four corners of the ground. Once the four corner stakes have been driven in, they must never be pulled out again."
The consecration of white mustard seeds is likewise performed; one should then pierce holes about one span deep in each of the four directions and in the center, and bury the mustard seeds therein.
Thereafter, having mixed cow dung with fragrant water, smear it upon the ground once more; having completed one application, perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) again.

Next, establish the *maṇḍala* (place of practice), making it as wide or narrow as desired, and suspend various banners, canopies, and precious objects to ensure it is most strictly purified. Perform the ritual of boundary-binding once more, then offer a small portion of flowers and incense to the deities of the path; having completed the practice, dismiss the Vajra-being.
Once the dismissal has been performed, one should construct a ritual altar (*dharmamaṇḍala*) measuring four cubits within the site of practice using five colors—namely:
first, white; second, yellow; third, red; fourth, blue; and fifth, black.

"When one wishes to construct the maṇḍala, further mix various kinds of fragrant incense with water, recite the Great Heart Mantra over the fragrant water one hundred and eight times, and use it to smear the ground."

Once the liquid has dried, one should immediately use chalk lines to demarcate the ground; having established the boundaries with equal sides and right angles, first apply white powder, then yellow, then red, then blue, and finally black.
"In the center of the maṇḍala, construct a lotus seat and install an image of the Vajra Cundī; on the eastern side, place three vajras;
the southern and northern sides are likewise as the eastern side; at each of the four corners, place two vajras, each intersecting the other like a cross;
within the western gate, place two vajras separately on both the north and south sides."

Upon each of these, place offerings of food and drink; these foods must consist of various kinds of cakes and fruits, fully arranged in ten plates—four plates on each of the four sides, four plates at the four corners, one plate in the center, and one plate placed outside—to be bestowed upon all the ghosts and spirits.

There should be fifty-two lamps; if these cannot be provided, sixteen may be used: place one lamp at each of the four corners of the center, one lamp at each of the four corners of the outer enclosure, and one lamp on each side of the four gates.
At each of the four corners, plant a large single-edged sword; at the center of each of the four gates, plant an arrow; and in the center, place a bright mirror facing upward.

The mantra-master sits at the western gate facing east; to the south of the mantra-master, set up a fire hearth for the purpose of burning clarified butter, honey, milk, curd, sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, and other such substances.
Once the mantra-practitioner has spread a clean cloth before him, he should place various kinds of incense, flowers, food, drink, and other offerings upon it.

When all have been arranged and the boundary (sīmā) has been further bound, the practitioner recites the mantra while sealing the incense burner with a mudrā. Holding the incense burner in his hand, he burns the incense and makes this formal declaration (*prārthanā*); the ritual application is as previously described. He then performs the rites of self-protection (*rakṣā*), expulsion (*vidhūnana*), boundary-binding, and invocation, following exactly what was explained previously for the Eleven-faced [Avalokiteśvara]. Holding the incense burner, he should first make offerings to Amitābha Buddha, and subsequently make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, and others of the eastern direction, as well as Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Great Kings; the same applies to the ten directions.

Having completed the general offerings, set down the incense burner and perform three prostrations with a sincere mind. Next, scatter all manner of exquisite incense and flowers; next, perform circumambulation; and next, offer oblations by burning ghee, honey, food, and other substances. If one lacks incense, flowers, food, or other such items for daily offerings, one should instead perform the "Seal of All Offerings" (Sarvapūjāmudrā) to make the offering.
"The mudrā is as previously described in the Prajñā section.
The mantra is:

'Oṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhite suparāhite gagana-khaṃ samate svāhā. Next, perform the Prajñā-mudrā, placing it at the heart; verbally confess and repent for the transgressions committed through the three karmas, then sit upright and remain motionless."
He prostrated to the Buddha again and again, praising him with his voice, saying:
"The wisdom of all Buddhas, their great courage and diligence, their Nārāyaṇa-like strength, and their practice of the perfections such as Prajñāpāramitā."
Next, make the vow, saying:

"May we, the disciples, if among humans, always hear the Mahāyāna Dharma and the treasury of teachings such as the dhāraṇīs and mudrās; may we not see evil things, not hear evil teachings, not encounter heretics or various wicked people, and not suffer the nine untimely deaths."
"At the time of death, one shall be reborn at will in the pure lands of the ten directions and constantly behold all Buddhas.
All sentient beings shall likewise be so.
Having formed this thought, recite the Great Heart Mantra one thousand and eight times, and perform the ritual mudrās of the respective division in succession as an offering.

"From this time forward, every morning after washing one's hands and face and finishing the cleansing of the teeth by chewing *śalākā* (willow twigs), one shall recite the *Suxin Zhou* (Heart Sūtra) seven times over water held in the hand and scatter it toward the east; this shall be done three times."

Thereafter, he should further consecrate the pure water in his hand seven times and sprinkle it over his head; subsequently, he should perform a ritual bath. If, due to specific circumstances, he is unable to bathe, he should simply perform the rite of sprinkling water to establish purity, and then enter his room.
"Once the protection of the body has been completed, enter the maṇḍala and perform offerings in this manner;
if you are unable to provide daily food and drink, it is also permissible to perform offerings using incense, flowers, and mudrās alone."

"One must perform offerings and repentance at one distinct time each night, and recite the mantra three times each day until a total of one million recitations are fulfilled. Once the count is complete, disperse the ritual altar and reapply the clay coating just as it was at the beginning."

Having performed the ritual procedures for the installation and the overnight offering, when the rites are concluded, lift the water jar from the center of the mandala and carry it outside the western gate of the practice hall.
Furthermore, construct another small square altar; place a small seat upon the altar and have the person receiving the dharma sit upon it, then pour water over the crown of the recipient's head.
At the time of the consecration, the recipient of the Dharma makes a vow with both mind and speech.

Once the consecration is completed, they don their robes and enter the inner maṇḍala, performing the mudrās and dispatching [the deities] one by one in sequence. Therefore, they will constantly receive the protective mindfulness of Cundāvajra, and all their ritual applications will possess spiritual efficacy.

The Ritual Altar for the Kuṇḍalī Vajra’s Method of Saving from Illness: “If there is someone afflicted by a disease caused by spirits or ghosts, one should first complete the ritual adornment of the *maṇḍala* at the patient’s home according to the Dharma. Then, having dressed the patron in fine garments, one should construct for them a four-cubit altar of two colors—one white and the other red.”
The maṇḍala shall have four gates, with two *vajras* drawn in each of the five directions, intersecting one another at right angles.
At each of the four corners of the maṇḍala, plant a long sword; at each of the four gates, plant a fine arrow; and in the center, place a mirror face upward.

Various kinds of food and drink were collectively placed in ten plates—four plates on each of the four sides, four plates at the four corners, one plate in the center, and one plate outside the altar—and offered to all the ghosts and spirits.
There shall be twelve lamps and one *sāla* tree with scented water.
Outside the altar, to the southwest, prepare a separate small circular earthen platform; place a dish of food and set down a lamp there to offer to all ghosts and spirits.
"At the center of the great maṇḍala, place a water jar filled with pure water; adorn its mouth with a bundle of fresh silk tied together with green cypress leaves and green willow leaves."

For a period of three days, one shall remain at the altar site and recite the aforementioned Great Mantra; the practice shall cease immediately once the patient has recovered. During this time, burn only *agaru* (aloe) incense.
If one does not recite the mantra, the patient shall return to his room;
if one is reciting the mantra, one shall remain within the altar enclosure.
The mantra master and the patient must both abstain from all alcohol, meat, and the five pungent vegetables; if they consume these, the ritual will not be accomplished.

If the practice is not performed according to the Dharma or is impure, both the mantra master and the patient will be struck by the demon king Vināyaka, such that he cannot be exorcised and the ritual will fail to take effect as originally intended.

"Recite the mantra seven times over all available incense, flowers, scented water, food, drink, and other items; likewise, recite it seven times over every object used within the mandala. Only after this may they be employed. If one acts in this manner, the ritual will be successfully accomplished."
"The method for curing diseases through the *Cundī-vajrī* employs the Great Heart Mantra, the Central Heart Mantra, and the Small Heart Mantra.
The Great Heart Mantra is as follows:
'Oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte huṃ phaṭ. The Central Heart Mantra is as follows:"
“Oṃ duna duna hana hana huṃ phaṭ. The minor heart-mantra is: “Oṃ amṛte huṃ phaṭ.
When Vajrapāñcika recited this mantra before the Buddha, all the ghosts and spirits were struck with trembling, and the earth shook throughout.

"If a person suffers from illness such that they vomit food and cannot swallow it, repeatedly bowing their head until they fall to the ground with dizziness, this is caused by the *vapuṣī* ghost entering the person's body to afflict them with disease. By mixing ghee with *sāra* resin incense and reciting the mantra over it seven times, one should burn it in fire and fumigate the patient's body; the illness will then be cured."

If the illness does not subside, recite the mantra over white mustard seeds seven times, circle them around the body seven times, and then burn them in fire; if one burns them in this manner twenty-one times, the illness will immediately be cured.
"One who performs this rite shall experience the Great Joy of Vajra.

If a person suffers from a mental affliction such that they run wild here and there, or sit while disrobed, or have their hair disheveled, or take up dust and soil to defile their body; or if they desire sexual intercourse, or eat repeatedly yet claim never to be full; or if they wish to strike one another, or wish to kill one another; or if they rush headlong into water or fire without avoidance, or fall directly into boiling water as soon as they approach it—if such various and manifold symptoms occur, one should know for certain that a ghost has entered their body and is causing these ailments."

At that time, the mantra-practitioner immediately constructs for him a water-maṇḍala two cubits in size; holding an incense burner in his hand, he makes offerings to all the Buddhas of the ten directions, burning both agallochum and frankincense—either one of these two types may be used.
If one forms the protection mudrā over the patient's head and recites the mantra repeatedly, the illness will be cured—should it not be cured in one day, it will be cured in two days.

"If one suffers from a wind-heat illness characterized by frequent agitation and alarm, coming and going with an unsettled mind, or repeatedly looking at women—whether they be beautiful or ugly—for such a patient, the disease will be cured by burning *sāla* tree incense while reciting the mantra. If this incense is unavailable, one should take ox-gallstone mixed with white mustard seeds and burn them while reciting the mantra, and the disease will likewise be cured. This medicine must always be carried on one's person."
"If this illness is caused by a demon sent by a heavenly deity, one will be cured immediately upon burning the incense before it."

“Regarding the ‘Smoke-Fire Ghost’ (dhūmaketu-piśāca): if there is a person who recites and maintains the mantras of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, Devas, and so forth, this ghost will constantly follow and watch for an opportunity to enter that person’s body. It causes their ritual activities to fail, makes them unattractive, and prevents various rites from succeeding. After the evening meal, one should take pure clarified butter (*ghṛta*) and light a single lamp. Recite the mantra twenty-one times and place this lamp at the foot of the bed. Cover the lamp with a bowl and step upon the bowl with the left foot while reciting the mantra seven times. Wherever one treats illness, one will not fear any ghosts or spirits, and they will be unable to create obstacles. If one does not perform this rite, it will cause the practitioner’s mind and intentions to become unstable and subject to change.”

"If a person suffers from the simultaneous discharge of tears, mucus, and saliva, or from making sounds while sleeping, such a patient should perform the aforementioned rite, and their illness will immediately be cured."

"If a messenger from the house of a patient comes to summon the mantra-master, and upon reaching the master’s presence, the master faces either southwest or northwest, the illness will not be cured and he must not go; the mantra-master shall not depart."

If you are summoned by a person of high status and must go against your will, form the protection-of-the-body mudrā yourself and recite the mantra twenty-one times with a sincere heart before departing. Upon arriving at that place, return immediately; do not linger further.
"If an ordinary person of low status does not go, that is best; if they go, it is of no benefit and one will lose one's reputation.

If a messenger from a patient's household arrives at the master's side and repeatedly rubs their face with their left hand, the incantation-master must not leave; if he leaves and does not return, whether the person is noble or lowly, the consequences are the same as previously described."
"The image of Skandha should be placed in the south, seated facing north.
The mantra-practitioner should sit opposite the image, facing south.

At the site for treating illness, construct a water-maṇḍala two cubits in size. In the center of this maṇḍala, place a single fire-pit. Recite the mantra over twenty-one *puṣpaka* flowers (in the Tang language, "flowers") and cast them into the fire. When one hundred and eight such offerings have been made, all illnesses and pains will be cured without exception."
One who performs this rite shall bind all ghosts and spirits, such that they dare not commit evil.

One must recite the mantra over water seven times; first, one must sprinkle it over the head of the practitioner seven times, and only after these seven repetitions should one proceed to the place where the patient lies.
Furthermore, if one recites the mantra over pure water twenty-one times and sprinkles it once upon the crown of a sick person's head, they will immediately recover.

"If a person suffers from blindness, take the resin of *karavīra* (in the language of Tang, *yang zhi du*) and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times; apply it to the eyes, and the person suffering from blindness will immediately regain their sight. If one gathers its leaves, the resinous juice will exude."

"Furthermore, there is another method: take four stakes made of khadira wood, each eight finger-widths long; recite the mantra over each stake twenty-one times, and then drive these stakes into the four corners of the patient's dwelling to establish a boundary."

If this wood is not available, recite the mantra over white mustard seeds twenty-one times and scatter them at the four corners and four sides of the patient’s residence; the ritual for binding is as before.
"If you wish to cure an illness, go to the patient's location and burn agalloch incense, reciting the mantra:
'Ha ha ha.'"
After he had rebuked him three times, the illness was immediately cured.

"If someone has been poisoned and the venom has entered their belly, one should take a knife in hand and recite the mantra with a sincere mind one hundred and eight times; then, by drawing upon that person's body from a distance with this knife, they will be healed."

"If one wishes to distance oneself from an enemy, one should recite the mantra over one hundred and eight pieces of cloth (pauṣpa) and, according to the previous ritual, burn one piece for each recitation before the image; that person will depart far away."
“Furthermore, there is another rite: on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should construct a water-maṇḍala four cubits in size near a window or door.
Within it, place an image and fashion a human figure out of clean clay, one cubit in height, lying supine with the head toward the south and the feet toward the north.”
Cast white mustard seeds into the fire while reciting the mantra, and simultaneously strike the effigy; thus one will immediately be able to drive [the affliction] far away at will.

If one wishes to restore that person to their former state, take white mustard seeds and *bhuspuṭa* (mustard seeds) and recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times. Cast them into sandalwood-scented perfumed water; having completed these one hundred and eight repetitions, call the person's name and say aloud:
"Be quickly cured!"
Reciting this once and invoking it once, one will immediately be cured.

If one seeks to treat *mīgu* (consumption), grind dried ginger (*śuṇṭhī*) and *pippalī*—translated into Chinese as *hujiao* (black pepper)—into a powder. Fashion a human figure (*manuṣya*) out of beeswax, place the aforementioned medicine inside its belly, and roast the human figure over a fire while reciting:
"Tsi-kā-lan tsi-kā-lan, Ā-i-shê ā-i-shê."
In this manner, perform the rite three times each day until the eighth day; this applies equally to both women and men alike—namely, for Āīśā.
"If one knows the location of a hidden treasure, one should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times at each of the three daily sessions for three days while striking the spot with a *vajra*.
By performing this rite, the treasure will emerge within three days;
if it does not emerge, a sound will arise from the very place struck, and by digging there, one shall obtain it."
If you do not know [the method], do not attempt it; if you do, you will fail and merely waste your effort.
If the hidden treasure does not emerge, perform the ritual for seven days while providing food and drink; by reciting the mantra, it will come forth.

"When one wishes to eat, before eating, one should offer various foods to Kuṇḍalī. Having set aside a small portion, one should secretly recite the heart-mantra of Kuṇḍalī seven times within the mind; then that Kuṇḍalī will constantly follow the mantra-practitioner wherever they go and provide protection in every respect."
"If one can perform this rite daily, Vajramuṇḍalī’s heart will be greatly delighted; she will never depart from afar and will protect one in all places, with great efficacy in curing diseases."

“If a domestic animal falls ill, one should take its bone according to its species, recite the mantra over it once, and cast it into fire to be burned; this should be done three times a day—at dawn, at dusk, and at midday—until the illness is cured.”

The Vajratāhasa Mudrā and Dhāraṇī Method (translated into Chinese as *Dàxiào Jīngāng*, "Great Laughter Vajra"). First, the Vajratāhasa Body Mudrā and Dhāraṇī, Number One: First, place the two middle fingers so that each presses against the back of its respective ring finger. The tips of the two ring fingers touch one another; the two little fingers are spread apart with their tips held straight upright, about one cun apart. The two thumbs press down on the side joints of the second phalanges of the two ring fingers. Join the wrists. The two index fingers are bent so that their tips touch, and the index fingers move back and forth.
The mantra is:

“Tadyathā | Oṃ | Vajratāhasanamahā | Khāhi khāhi | Svāhā. 2. The Body-Seal (Kāyamudrā), second. 3. The Mudrā for Binding the Boundary (Sīmābandhana-mudrā), Number Three. First, with the middle finger, ring finger, and index finger of the right hand, hook the ring finger, middle finger, and index finger of the left hand. Each of the two thumbs presses down upon the nails of the respective little fingers. Recite the Body Mantra while sealing the water with this mudrā. After reciting it seven times, sprinkle it throughout the ten directions to universally bind the boundary; this is called the Great Binding of the Boundary.

4. The Mudrā for Expelling Vināyakas, the Fourth. "Following the previous *sīmā-bandhana* mudrā, hook the two little fingers together with their tips facing outward; move the two thumbs so that they press upon the tips of the nails of the [opposing] index fingers. “Svāhā,” one hundred and fifty times. Regarding this dhāraṇī method, it is said:

Having completed various offerings of incense and flowers before a śarīra stūpa, wait for the time of a solar or lunar eclipse and recite this Vajratāhasa dhāraṇī until the sun or moon returns to its former state, after which you may cease. This rite will then be accomplished; whatever one seeks, by reciting it, all shall be attained according to one’s wishes and fruits.
"If a person wishes to perform the *sarvabuddhaviśodhana-hūṃ*, they should construct a five-colored mandala that is perfectly square, four cubits in length and breadth.
Having smeared the ground with cow dung to purify the mandala, they should burn agalloch incense and scatter various kinds of flowers."
Having completed the offerings, have a young boy sit before this altar and recite this mantra; any doubts concerning the matter will then be resolved.

"If all manner of evil winds or calamitous hail and rain damage the five grains, grasp the vajra and recite the mantra continuously while pointing it toward them from afar as if to strike; they shall cease immediately."
The mantra-practitioner must not recite with a mind of great anger, intending to crush and destroy that evil dragon and its retinue.
Furthermore, when this mantra is maintained according to the Dharma, the rājas will respect and have faith, relinquishing their wealth to cultivate merit.
When performing this rite, take one of the three types of trees—the Pippala, the Nyagrodha, or the Udumbara—and cut a piece one cubit in length; then kindle this wood with fire.

Take white mustard seeds and mix them with clarified butter; having recited the mantra once, cast them into the fire. If one continues in this manner for three days and three nights, one will achieve accomplishment, becoming endowed with majestic power, loved and respected by all people, and receiving their offerings.
When burning this wood, one should construct a well-railing; these three types of wood all have white sap and are called *rājabhṛṅgarāja*, which in the language of Tang means "King Tree.
If one wishes to seek wealth and goods, one should mix *sumana* flowers with clarified butter (*sarpis*) and burn them while reciting the mantra; one will then obtain wild objects from the earth.
If his mind reaches its goal, he will also see hidden treasures, or he will see the location of those objects in a dream.

"If one wishes to subdue all wicked people and enemies, one should take earth from the intersection of a crossroads, mix it with white mustard seeds, and perform the incantation while burning them for one day and one night; then all enemies will become joyful, and there will be none who do not submit."
"Furthermore, regarding all types of insanity: recite the mantra over black sheep's wool and have a pure young girl spin this wool to make a consecrated cord.
Once the cord has been knotted with the mantra, tie it upon the patient's head; all forms of insanity shall be cured immediately."

Furthermore, to cure all diseases caused by *yacodaka*, wild-path spirits, cat-spirits (*māyā-ghora*), and the like: knead flour with water to form a human effigy, and while reciting the mantra continuously, sever that figure with a vajra-staff, scattering it piece by piece. Then, burn *guggulu* incense; all disturbances and afflictions caused by *yacodaka* spirits will be utterly destroyed, and they shall be unable to cause harm.

Furthermore, for those afflicted by all kinds of *gudu* poisons or medicinal toxins, or those who are human beings on the verge of death, one should take a vajra staff and recite the mantra over water three times; if administered to them, they will immediately recover.

Furthermore, if a person suffers from various malignant sores, such as leaking ulcers, pustules, erysipelas, or scabies, they should take white earth to draw a maṇḍala and recite the mantra continuously. By dividing and breaking apart this maṇḍala, all malignant sores will be completely healed.

Furthermore, when all kinds of vetāla-demons cause illness, one should burn agallochum incense, consecrate black sheep’s wool with mantras, fashion it into a cord, tie it into knots, and fasten it around the patient's neck.
Furthermore, when one recites the mantra over the ear canals of a sick person, they immediately attain liberation.

If the illness does not subside, one may again recite the mantra with a mind of wrath while striking the ground with a vajra-staff; all the ghosts who have caused the illness will then come forward to submit, join their palms, and beg for their lives, saying:
"Do not strike us further! Today our bodies and minds suffer the agony of broken limbs; we only pray that you release us, for we dare not come again."

"Furthermore, if one wishes to master all sutras and treatises, as well as all arts and crafts, one should recite this mantra once every morning upon rising; by maintaining an uninterrupted focus of the mind, the method will be accomplished."
One day he was able to recite five hundred verses of scripture; whatever he sought, if he recited with fierce wrath, there was nothing that was not fulfilled.

"The vajra is nine finger-widths wide and long; it may be made of red copper, white sandalwood, or the heartwood of jujube wood—any one of these will suffice, though among them, red sandalwood is the most excellent."
"The efficacy of the Vajratāṣa is such that the diseases it treats are like snow melted by hot water, or like dry grass consumed by a fierce fire."

Chapter on the Dharma-Seals and Mantras of Vajroṣṇīṣa, Part 1: The Dharma-Seal and Mantra for Vajroṣṇīṣa’s Body Protection. First:

The Dharma-Seal and Mantra for Vajroṣṇīṣa’s Body Protection (in Chinese: *Bùjìngjié Jīngāng*; there are seventeen seals and forty-two mantras). [Method: Place both palms facing the body. Interlace the middle fingers and ring fingers, pressing their tips against the palms. Hold the little fingers upright and askew, with their tips touching one another. Bend the two index fingers and hook them together, with the right pressing down upon the left. Bend the two thumbs and press them against the transverse creases at the upper joints of the index fingers.
The mantra is:

"Oṃ vajra-kuruta mahā-sara hana-daha paca vidambaya ucchuṣma kuruta huṃ phaṭ. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If a person wishes to perform rites concerning the head of fire, they must first protect their body by reciting this seal-mantra seven times; thereafter, when they employ the Ucchuṣma rite, it shall be entirely efficacious.
"Use this seal and mantra to cure all illnesses; recite it one hundred thousand times before putting it into practice. 2.

The Body Seal and Mantra of Ucchuṣma (The Second) With the ring finger and little finger of the right hand, enter from behind the ring finger of the left hand into the space between the middle finger and the ring finger. Press the tips of the right thumb against the nails of the right ring finger and little finger, and grasp the left ring finger and little finger. Next, bend the left ring finger and little finger, and again press the tips of the left thumb against the nails of the left ring finger and little finger, forming a circular hook. Straighten both index fingers and middle fingers so that their tips touch, and move the index fingers back and forth."
The mantra is as follows:

“Oṃ vajra-krodha mahābala hana daha paca vikira vidambaya jaṭhara lambodara ucchuṣma krodha huṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. When entering the maṇḍala to perform the ritual, one should daily make offerings; having protected the body and bound the boundary with this seal, one then uses this same seal to invoke and invite the Vajra.

"If you wish to obtain a sign of efficacy, burn agalloch incense in a pure place and recite this mantra for seven days and seven nights; once ten thousand recitations are completed, all shall be proven effective."

It is also effective when used concurrently for treating illnesses. Regarding the times for treating illness: recite one thousand and eight times during each of the three periods—once at dawn, once at midday, and once at dusk. Do this every day; alternatively, it is also acceptable to recite one hundred and eight times. Apart from these three periods, you must not recite recklessly.

"When reciting and maintaining [the mantra], it is better to do so without counting the repetitions; this will bring about additional blessings. Furthermore, within one hundred days, you must not stay overnight outside the ritual precinct, engage in sexual intercourse, or violate the precepts."
If one breaks the precepts, the various deities will not protect them nor assist them with their power, and there will be no great efficacy.
When intending to go out for the purpose of defecating or urinating, do not wear clean robes while entering the latrine;
the same applies when eating.

If one has finished defecating, urinating, or eating, one must necessarily bathe with fragrant water until clean, then put on pure garments and enter the *maṇḍala* to recite and maintain the *Mūla-karma*.
"If one wishes to behold Vajra in person when making a petition, and performs the ritual for the delight of Cundī every night, one will certainly see him."
When the practitioner beholds the vajra, they must not give rise to fear.
If the mind is terrified, it will cause that person to lose their composure and become distraught. Why is this so?

If that person is able to attain the vajra, they will be able to subjugate all ghosts and spirits; therefore, when all those ghosts and spirits see him on the verge of achieving great spiritual efficacy, they come to terrify him, causing his practice to fail and regress.
One must strengthen the heart and make one’s resolve firm, so that the mind does not waver.
To seek the realization of the Dharma of the Body, follow what is explained below:

"This mantra was spoken with one voice by all the eight classes of spirits who have gathered together. Regardless of whether it is auspicious or inauspicious, during the bright or dark fortnights, whether one is observing a fast or not, whether one is pure or impure, or whether one has eaten or not—if one first recites this mantra one hundred thousand times, the Dharma will be accomplished, and one shall gain power in all that is sought."

Furthermore, kindle a fire using fuel sticks of *śvetajatu* wood; then take fine branches of this same wood and cut them into one thousand and eight pieces of any desired length. Recite the mantra over each piece together with white mustard seeds once, and cast them into the fire. When these one thousand and eight repetitions are completed, one will attain noble and superior status, and even the heavenly kings above will all be filled with joy.

"Furthermore, according to another method, whether one is pure or impure, and whether by day or by night, if one recites the mantra three hundred thousand times, there will be no obstacles whatsoever in any place."

Continue to mix sesame seeds with clarified butter, stirring them together; taking a small portion, recite the mantra once and cast it into the fire. When this has been done one thousand and eight times, the ritual of the mantra will be accomplished.

"Furthermore, according to another method, if one recites this mantra one hundred thousand times atop a high mountain peak, then wherever one goes, by merely making the sound 'hūṃ hūṃ' and snapping one's fingers, no evil person will be able to confront them or create obstacles and afflictions."

"Furthermore, according to this method, if one recites [the mantra] one hundred and eight times each during the three periods of dawn, midday, and dusk every day, then while sleeping at night, all devas will protect one, and all people will also constantly cherish and remember one."

"Furthermore, regarding the method for all illnesses caused by ghosts and spirits: take a branch of a pomegranate tree and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times; strike the patient with it, and the illness will immediately be cured."

3. The Dharani and Seal for the Boundary-binding of Ucchuṣma, Third. "Follow the previous Great Body-protection Seal; however, extend the two index fingers so that they are separated by about three finger-widths behind the middle fingers."
The mantra is:

“Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye | mahāyakṣasenāpate | tadyathā | oṃ sarvavisara | nivartaya | natha natha | sarvavisara | gavi gavi | ācchedika | saṃvartana | svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If performing ritual acts, one should bind the boundaries of the four directions, above, below, and the intermediate spaces with this seal, reciting the mantra twenty-one times.
"If one uses this dharma to treat illness, recite the mantra twenty-one times and snap the fingers likewise twenty-one times; there will be a verified efficacy in removing the disease.

If a person is startled or terrified while lying down at night, they should also perform the aforementioned method by reciting the mantra twenty-one times and snapping their fingers twenty-one times; the sleeper will never again experience such terror."

4. The Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the Joyful Dharma of Ucchuṣma. The fourth [section], "The Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the Joyful Dharma of Ucchuṣma": "With the left hand, bend the thumb over the fingers so that its tip rests against the third joint of the ring finger; form a fist with the remaining four fingers."
The mantra is:

“Oṃ, śabarā, śabarā, saṅgamaya, saṅgamaya, karakara, varavara, harahara, sarasara, parapara, jarajara, mara-mara, sarasara, svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one performs the ritual of the Fire-Head Vajra (*Agnimukha-vajra*), when reciting the mantra to protect the body and bind the boundary (*rakṣā-sīmābandha*), and to invoke and install the Fire-Head Vajra, one should first perform this mudrā and recite the mantra; thus, all shall be made joyful.
"If there is anyone afflicted with a malignant ulcer, by rubbing this seal upon the ulcer while reciting the mantra, that ulcer will immediately heal.
By maintaining this seal and mantra, one will encounter no obstacles wherever one goes, and all people who see one will rejoice."
"If one has consumed poison, one should form this mudrā around the body and above the head; by reciting the mantra, the ailment will be cured immediately.

5. The Mudrā and Mantra for the Ritual Offering to Ucchuṣma. Fifth: "Following the previous body-mudrā, change only this: join the two index fingers so that they press against the upper edge of the middle fingernails."
The mantra is as follows:

“Oṃ vajra-kuruta mahāphala oṃ jvāla jvāla mahājvāla cūḍa cūḍa khira khira sara sara hara hara dhaka dhaka svāhā. This is the Dharma-seal mantra. If one wishes to perform ritual acts and invoke the Fire-Head Vajra for installation, one should form this seal and recite the mantra while making offerings; thus one will immediately obtain various benefits and efficacious results.

6. The Seal and Mantra for Healing Ghostly Illnesses by Ucchuṣma, Number Six; also known as the Seal and Mantra for Slaying Ghosts. "Follow the previous body seal, with this modification: turn the right index finger and middle finger inward and rub them against the tips of the left index finger and middle finger."
The mantra is:

“Oṃ vatsara-kuruta mahā-bala raudra-viśruta śarīrāya chinda chinda hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. When a mantra-reciter wishes to depart to treat an illness, he should first take pure ashes with the ring finger and thumb of his right hand, recite this mantra over them seven times, and then apply them to his own crown, the space between his eyebrows, his throat, his left shoulder, his right shoulder, and his heart center. Having thus protected himself, he may depart.

Once the illness has been cured, one should then perform the rite of protecting the body upon that patient according to the method previously described; thus, the disease-demon will be unable to approach the patient’s side, nor will it be able to enter the threshold of his house.

7. The Dharma Seal and Mantra of Ucchuṣmavajra. Regarding the Dharma Seal and Mantra of Ucchuṣmavajra, the seventh: "Following the previous body seal, change only this: bend the two index fingers and each extend them downward into the palms."
The mantra says: "Oṃ vajra..."
