"For one who recites this mantra, all mantra-empowerments will swiftly be accomplished; all virtuous deeds will be achieved according to one's intentions; and all matters of aspiration will be fulfilled as desired."

"If the aforementioned superior rites do not succeed as desired, the mantra-practitioner should know that there are certainly obstacles present. Then, during either the waxing or waning moon, on the eighth or fifteenth day, one should smear the ground with cow dung, prepare offerings of food, drink, flowers, and fruits, and burn agalloch incense. Taking white thread, one should recite the mantra over it once for each knot; having thus made forty-nine knots, one should tie them around the left arm. All obstructing spirits and demons will then be completely bound, and they shall no longer be able to create obstacles or hinder the fundamental practice."

"If a person wishes to travel east or west on a long journey, they should first prepare a water altar and invoke Mārīcī to be installed there. Taking rice grains and flowers mixed with ghee and honey, they should offer them into the fire one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra. Whoever then departs for their desired destination will meet with great auspiciousness and attain powerful spiritual efficacy."
Furthermore, there is another method: for seven days, construct a water altar each day and summon Mārīcī to be installed there.
Additionally, set up a fire pit and kindle a fire of *śāla* wood; within that fire, burn non-glutinous rice and sesame seeds one hundred and eight times while reciting the mantra.

Three times each day, recite this one hundred and eight times per session; when this practice has been completed for seven days, those who approach the king and his ministers will be met with their favor.

“There is yet another rite: if you wish to engage in debate, follow the previous method by burning one hundred and eight segments of *bīja* branches, each one foot long, while reciting mantras. If one performs this rite for seven days in this manner, one will become a master debater of great intelligence.”

"Furthermore, if one wishes to go into the mountains, one should follow the previous method and burn ghee one hundred and eight times while reciting the mantra; then no birds, beasts, or venomous insects shall be able to cause harm."

"Furthermore, according to another method, if a person wishes to see Mārīcī, they should follow the previous ritual: kindle a fire using fuel sticks of *śāli* grain wood, take twenty-one pieces of celestial *agaru* incense, smear them with ghee, honey, and curd, and burn them while reciting the mantra twenty-one times."

Day after day, he consumed only three things—polished rice, cooked rice, and milk curds—and was not permitted to eat anything else; yet throughout the seven days, his daily offerings were increasingly superior in variety.
When this rite was performed in this manner for seven days, on the seventh day, the body of Mārīcī appeared within the maṇḍala and addressed the practitioner, saying: "O [Name]!"
"What vow do you now wish to seek?

At that time, the practitioner answers according to his own will; when Mārīcī grants permission and departs after bestowing the boon, one immediately knows that the efficacy has been attained, and all the devas rejoice.

"Furthermore, according to another method, during the seven days, three times each day, one should burn the three substances—mimosa grass, white calamus, and white mustard seeds—with fire while reciting the mantra. Having done so, one approaches the Rāja, and the person will be pleased."

"Furthermore, regarding the method for approaching officials: following the previous rite, burn white mustard seeds while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day. For seven days, consume only three things—polished rice, milk, and curd—and do not eat anything else. When these seven days have concluded, if you approach the official, that person will be pleased."

Furthermore, if one wishes to rely on the previous method, burning *bimba* leaves three times each day with one hundred and eight recitations of the mantra for each occasion, and continuing thus for seven full days, it will be highly effective in treating all illnesses caused by malevolent spirits.

"Furthermore, according to the same method as before, take high-quality barley, remove the husks, and pound it finely to make a powder. Mix this with honey to form one hundred and eight pellets, each the size of a plum."
During the seven days, the practitioner shall abstain from all food on the first day; for the remaining six days, one may eat as desired.
Every day, one should take the parched barley that has been scorched by fire, recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times, and form the *uttama-harṣa-mudrā* (the seal of supreme joy).
When one hundred and eight such bundles have been completely burned, extinguish the fire with water and fumigate both palms over the smoke. Recite the mantra twenty-one times, making this aspiration:
"May my hands perform all rites and achieve various efficacious results."
All these shall be verified, and the person before you will rejoice.

Furthermore, according to another method, if one burns *āmalaka* leaves one hundred and eight times while reciting the mantra as previously described, it cures all demonic illnesses, and the patient shall recover through the power of the mantra.

"Furthermore, according to another method: if a person suffers from a feverish illness, take some fine green grass and hold it to the mouth; recite the mantra twenty-one times and rub it upon the patient fifty-four times. Both the practitioner and the patient will then be cured."
"Furthermore, according to another method, if one recites the mantra once or three times at each of the three periods of the day, it constitutes a great protection of the body;
if three times, it constitutes a great boundary-binding (*mahā-sīmābandha*);
and for one who recites the mantra five times, whatever beloved human beings they desire shall be obtained at will."
Recite the mantra six times to protect the body and establish a boundary; thus, one will have no fear when entering cemeteries at night. Furthermore, there is another method:

if one wishes to travel a long distance, first burn *guggulu* incense seven times in a private room while reciting the mantra. When setting out on the road, if the practitioner recites the mantra repeatedly, any encounters with bandits, ghosts, or other such perils along the way shall not approach them; they will all naturally depart from the person.

"Furthermore, according to another method, on the eighth day of the preceding waxing moon, within a clean chamber, take fine incense, flowers, and a small amount of non-glutinous rice, and burn them in fire while reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times."
The practitioner shall fast for one day and don clean, pure garments.
One who departs having performed this rite will be honored, respected, and provided with offerings by others; all ghosts and spirits likewise shall stand in awe and reverence.

"Furthermore, there is another method: take cow dung—collect it with a vessel before it has fallen to the ground so that it does not touch the earth—and immediately mix it with water to create a water-mandala. At the center of this mandala, place an image of the Buddha or a relic of the Buddha."

Having collected the milk of a mother cow and her calf, as well as that of a yellow cow, he made ghee; he placed it in a golden bowl and stirred the ghee with the ring finger of his right hand while reciting mantras.
If fire should emerge from atop the ghee, one should know for oneself that one will attain great intelligence;
one can then recite a thousand verses in a single day. If fire does not emerge, but there is only smoke and warmth, it indicates minor intelligence.

If neither smoke nor warmth is produced, one should prostrate oneself on the ground, place the mouth near the vessel of ghee, and use the ring finger of the right hand as a spoon to eat the ghee; thus, one will attain a small measure of intelligence.

"Furthermore, according to another method, one should prepare a four-cubit altar on well-tilled ground outside the eastern gate of the city. Taking five bricks or tiles, place one in the center and one on each of the four sides."
Furthermore, take four water jars filled with water and seal their mouths with willow branches; place them upon bricks on the four sides.
Then, take red sandalwood and grind it in water, and immediately sprinkle that water upon the altar.

Furthermore, one should offer red flowers to the altar; place four pieces of *hūyāñji* (antimony) beside each of the four water jars; encircle the four sides of the altar with five-colored thread; and outside the four sides of the altar, present various kinds of incense, flowers, food, and drink as offerings to the spirits and deities.

At the western gate of the maṇḍala, spread a seat of fresh green grass. The mantra-practitioner, wearing fine and pure garments, sits upon the green grass in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka), invokes Mārīcī and her various messengers, and arranges diverse offerings.
The mantra-practitioner holds green grass in his hand and recites the mantra while rubbing it from the crown of his head down to his feet one hundred and eight times.

The practitioner forms the Mārīcī-body mudrā with his hands; while holding the green grass within the mudrā, he places it upon his own crown. He then dispatches a disciple to take four water jars from the altar and pour them one by one over the practitioner’s head. Once this is completed, the practitioner puts on clean, pure garments, performs the protection-body mudrā, recollects the Buddha, and pays homage to the Buddha.

Having completed the ritual for Mārīcī, take three substances—nāgakeśara flowers, nāgakesara incense, and ghee—and for seven days, the mantra-practitioner shall consume only non-glutinous rice, cow’s milk, and gruel, and must not eat anything else. Day after day, one should recite the mantra over these three medicinal substances one hundred and eight times. On the seventh day, by applying those substances to one's own crown, right shoulder, left shoulder, heart, throat, and forehead, the efficacy will be realized; this instruction is not subject to exception.

Furthermore, according to another method, following the previous procedure, if a person suffers from hemorrhoids, one should take black thread to fashion a consecrated cord. Have the patient lie on a bed with their head to the east and feet to the west, and bind the patient’s waist with this consecrated cord. Then, using another consecrated cord, bind the legs of the bed and recite the mantra over them. If one performs this rite and recites the mantra twenty-one times in this manner, the hemorrhoids will be cured immediately.

"Furthermore, there is another method: if a person suffers from ailments of the neck, the treatment is as described above; the only difference is that instead of the previously mentioned waist-cord, one should bind it around the neck.

Another method: if a household is plagued by malevolent spirits, violent disturbances, epidemics, or incessant death, or if one seeks superior blessings but fails to obtain one's wishes, one should take earth from both banks of a river and fashion one hundred images of ghosts."

Among them, there is a king of ghosts named Vināyaka; this king of ghosts has the head of a white elephant, while the heads of the other ghosts are each fashioned in the forms of various birds and beasts. Their bodies, hands, and feet are all made in human form, with a height of approximately four or eight finger-widths.
Take red sandalwood and grind it in water; using this liquid mixed with clay, smear it upon the ground to construct an altar.
Upon the altar, fashion seats for the spirits using soil of five colors: one seat in the center, two in the north, two in the south, two in the east, and one in the west.
Place an image of the King of Ghosts upon the central seat, and distribute images of the ninety-nine ghosts among the remaining six seats.
Offer various kinds of incense, flowers, lamps—including seven butter lamps—and food and drink; furthermore, take guggulu incense mixed with clarified butter and burn it as an offering.
"The mantra-master sits at the western gate facing east, recites the Mārīcī-mantra seven times, and consecrates a thread of five colors twenty-one times with the mantra."

Thereafter, take the images of the various spirits from the three sides within the altar and gather them together at the center beside the King of Spirits; place them all in one spot and bind the hundred spirit-images together with a single thread of five colors. Then, take one hundred and eight lumps of calf dung, burning each one in the fire while reciting the mantra.
When burning each ball, recite the mantra *svāhā* once. First, proclaim:
"Bind all ghosts," and then say:

" Svāhā. "In this manner, once each person has finished offering one hundred and eight morsels, they shall then dig a hole in the ground to a depth reaching the waist, create an opening, and place within it the effigies of the bound ghosts along with the altar offerings and food. They shall then make offerings of various fragrant flowers and diverse foods to those ghosts, after which they shall fill the opening with earth, level the ground, and never emerge from there again."
"If, at the time when the mantrika’s karmic illness approaches death, he performs the visualization of 'releasing' within his mind, that ghost will be liberated.
If one performs this rite, Mārīcī will immediately appear; it is swift and brings great efficacy."
"Furthermore, after finishing the recitation of the mantra at the aforementioned water altar, do not speak with anyone and immediately enter your room to lie down.
If you experience extraordinary visions during the night, do not speak of them to others; discuss their goodness or evil only between the master and disciple.
After completing one hundred thousand recitations, if no such visions occur, take rice blossoms mixed with sesame seeds and perform the incense offering according to the previous ritual."

Furthermore, there will be no sensory realms, and one will no longer require food or drink; one need only scatter flowers and recite mantras. On the eighth, fifteenth, and twenty-third days of each month, offer whatever the mantra-master eats as a tribute. By reciting the mantras continuously, reproaching oneself, and repenting, one will surely obtain their wishes.
After the first three seven-day periods, one should test the power of the mantra once every seven days to know whether there is gradual progress.

Furthermore, according to another method, if throughout one's life one eats only rice and milk porridge daily and recites the mantra repeatedly, one will attain great intelligence and be deeply cherished by the Brahmins among the four castes;
if one consumes ghee, curd, and milk while burning [incense], one will be cherished by the Kṣatriyas.
If the fire burns barley, curd, or milk, the Vaiśyas will show affection;
if it burns sesame dregs, the Śūdras will show affection.

Furthermore, according to another method, if a person afflicted by demonic illness has their mouth closed and cannot speak, one should recite the mantra over water twenty-one times and blow it into the mouth seven times, and they will immediately speak.

"Furthermore, regarding the method for those afflicted by ghostly illnesses who have their mouths closed and cannot speak: take a corner of a *kāṣāya* robe and recite the mantra twenty-one times over it; strike them with it and they will immediately speak. Furthermore, regarding another method:

with the right hand, pinch ash between the thumb and the ring finger, recite the mantra seven times over it, and scatter it in the four directions; this will immediately establish a boundary (*sīmābandha*)."

"Furthermore, there is another method: fashion ten clay pellets and cast each one toward one of the four directions to establish a great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*). The extent of the boundary is determined by how far each pellet is thrown."

"Furthermore, there is a method: if a woman experiences difficult labor, recite the mantra over sesame oil seven times and rub it upon her navel; she will then give birth to a child. Furthermore, there is a method:

when one has gained the upper hand in a debate and is met with resentment by the opponent, or when one is slandered by another, or when engaged in a dispute and slandered by an adversary, or when being interrogated by an official regarding the truth or falsehood of a crime while bound in shackles—take white kusha root, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and tie it on the right arm. Then, forming the *mudrā* of joy (*ānandamudrā*) with the left hand and reciting the mantra, one who departs [with this] shall immediately attain the principle of great victory."
If one recites the mantra repeatedly, various efficacious results will be obtained.

Furthermore, there is another method: if a person has been stung by a venomous insect, the mantra-master should take thread of five colors and fashion a "mantra-rope" with twenty-one knots, over which he recites the mantra. Having tied it upon his own right arm, he proceeds to the side of the person who was stung; taking a willow branch and consecrating it with the mantra, he repeatedly rubs the person with his hand, and they will immediately recover.

"Furthermore, there is another method: if a person is bitten by a venomous snake and is on the verge of death, the mantra-master shall take water in his own cupped hands, recite the mantra over it seven times while holding it to his mouth, and then sprinkle that water upon the patient twenty-one times; with the mantra, the patient will immediately recover."
"Furthermore, according to another method: if one recites the mantra one hundred and eight times over fire while burning ghee, no birds, beasts, or venomous insects shall be able to cause harm.

Furthermore, according to another method: if a person develops a malignant ulcer, one should mix yellow earth with mud and apply it over the ulcer twenty-one times while reciting the mantra; the affliction will then be cured."

"Furthermore, according to another method, if an animal contracts an epidemic disease, one should kindle a fire of grain-wood and fuel at the very center of a city, village, or ward. By burning cow’s milk in the fire while reciting the mantra, the illness will be cured; this rite should be performed at night."

On the following day at noon, again kindle a fire with wood from the *rakta-śāla* tree; take white mustard seed oil and mix it with white mustard seeds, and burn them over the fire one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra. Then, [the patient] will be greatly cured.

"Furthermore, there is another method: take one thousand and eight pieces of *kairava* wood—this wood resembles the bodhi tree—and after consecrating each one individually, burn them completely in the fire while reciting the mantra once for each. All *kumbhāṇḍas*, *yakṣas*, and other spirits will be entirely delighted."
"Furthermore, according to another method: if one burns small pieces of winter melon in a fire one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra, all *piśācas* will be entirely delighted.

Furthermore, according to another method: if one takes one thousand and eight segments of wood from a cemetery and mixes them with sesame seeds, burning them in a fire one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra, all greatly malevolent spirits and deities will be delighted."

"Furthermore, according to another method: if one takes one thousand and eight segments of a Bodhi tree branch, anoints each one with ghee, and burns them one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra, the Four Great Heavenly Kings will rejoice and hold one in loving remembrance."

"Furthermore, according to another method: if there is one suffering from epilepsy, the mantra-master takes all five grains, mixes them together, scoops them up with his hands, and recites the mantra over them while burning them in fire. If he does this one thousand and eight times, the ghosts and spirits will rejoice, and the illness will be cured immediately."

"Furthermore, according to another method: if one takes *guggulu* incense, grinds it into pills, coats them with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), and burns them one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra, Maheśvara and all the attendant deities will be filled with joy."

"If one follows the previous ritual, constructs a water mandala, and performs various offerings, placing an image of the Buddha or relics of the Buddha at the center of the mandala; then, taking three thousand and eight pieces of *lākṣā* (*śamī-dāru*)—this being another name for the Bodhi tree—and coating each with curd, ghee, and honey, one burns them one by one in the fire, reciting the mantra once for each piece, until all three thousand and eight pieces have been exhausted."
One who performs this rite shall eliminate the five heinous crimes (*ānantarya*) and the four grave offenses (*pārājika*), attaining purity as well as the efficacy of the mantra.

Furthermore, if a practitioner follows the previous method to construct a water mandala and so forth, from the eighth day to the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, taking one thousand and eight pieces of *śiṃśapā* wood each day, anointing each piece with ghee and burning them while reciting the mantra, Mārīcī will enter the ritual arena and fulfill all their wishes.
If the practitioner beholds the body of Mārīcī with their own eyes, they shall obtain great spiritual efficacy.

Should she not appear, they must sincerely repent and yearn for Mārīcīdevī with deep longing; by fasting for one day and making various kinds of offerings, she will certainly manifest her form, and the practitioner shall obtain the various great efficacies of Mārīcī.

Furthermore, regarding the method for obtaining wealth: if one desires to acquire money and goods, during the two days from the fourteenth to the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should take sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, and paddy flowers at three sessions each day and burn them in the fire while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times. One will then obtain wealth that accords with one's heart's desire.

"Furthermore, according to another method: if one wishes to bind Māra, for seven days one should take one thousand and eight segments of *kṛtavedhana* tree branches—[one version says: *bodhi* tree branches]—each day. Having anointed each segment with white mustard seed oil, one should recite the mantra once over each and burn them in the fire; thus one will immediately bind Māra."

"Furthermore, according to another method, if a mantra-practitioner or a layperson, while performing this rite of incantation, is seized, arrested, taken away, or bound with shackles and fetters, they shall recite this mantra repeatedly; then the bonds will never hold."

"Furthermore, according to another method: if one wishes to obtain *śarāka*, for seven days, at the three periods of each day, take fragrant incense, grind it, and form it into one thousand and eight pills. Anoint each pill with ghee and burn them while reciting the mantra; the one who departs will then have their wish fulfilled."

"Furthermore, according to another method: if people are angry with one another, one should take sesame oil dregs mixed with rice husks and burn them over fire one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra; the other person will then become joyful."
"Furthermore, according to another method: if one takes sesame seeds and burns them one thousand and eight times while reciting the mantra, the person before one will love, cherish, and rejoice.

Furthermore, according to another method: if one wishes to obtain wealth, for seven days one should take one stalk of *kuci* grass (also called *gouluo* grass) each day—stalks six finger-widths long—and divide them into one thousand and eight segments; if one burns each segment in the fire while reciting the mantra, one will immediately obtain wealth."

"Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to seek a cherished object from another, one should take white calamus and recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times. By tying it upon one's own arm, one may go and beg for it, and there shall be nothing that cannot be obtained."

"Furthermore, there is another method: for twenty-one days—three times each day—take *guggulu* incense and pound it into one thousand and eight pills. Dip each pill into a mixture of curd, ghee, and honey, burn them one by one in the fire while reciting the mantra. If you go before a king or an official, that person will be filled with joy and hold you in affectionate regard."

"Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to become a *vilāsin*—in the Sanskrit sound this means 'steward' (*kangwei*)—one should, for seven days, take various famous incenses at the three periods of each day and pound them into one thousand and eight pills. By burning each pill with ghee while reciting the mantra, one will immediately fulfill one's wish."

"Furthermore, according to another method: if a practitioner bathes, enters the *maṇḍala*, and performs various offerings such as constructing a water altar (*toyamaṇḍala*), they should summon Mārīcī and establish her there. Reciting the mantra daily in this manner for one hundred thousand times, without interruption for seven days, [will bring success]."

When this rite is completed, one then says "I bind the boundary" (*sīmābandha*) aloud once, and it is accomplished—no hand gestures (*mudrā*), mantras, or ashes should be used. According to the practitioner’s wishes, all shall be achieved; no calamities shall approach their person. It can destroy the ritual works of others, as well as those of hostile persons, heretics (*tīrthika*), and the like. Thus, through the sovereign power of the celestial mantra’s spiritual efficacy, such results are brought about.
At that time, the goddess Mārīcī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
I possess a distinct dharma which I now wish to proclaim."
"Use red sandalwood three finger-widths wide and three inches long; on one side of the wood, carve an image of Mārīcī, resembling the form of a celestial maiden (devakanyā).
On either side of the image, carve attendants of Mārīcī, also resembling the forms of celestial maidens."
Furthermore, fashion a cover from separate red sandalwood wood and place it over the image.

Once this image has been made, if you wish to travel a long distance and intend to carry this image with you without separating it from yourself, conceal it in a hidden place so that no one knows of it, and recite the mantra repeatedly.
"If one has a wish, one should immediately construct a water maṇḍala; place an image at the center of the maṇḍala, summon Mārīcī and install her there, and make various offerings."
Furthermore, take one hundred and eight lotus flowers to offer as an act of worship.
Regarding the method of offering: take each lotus flower one by one with the hand, recite the mantra over each one, and thereby present them as an offering.
Furthermore, having burned sesame seeds and non-glutinous rice one thousand and eight times with fire while reciting the mantra, various efficacious results will be obtained when carrying the image.
The note states:
"All the aforementioned methods involve performing various offerings, such as water mandalas, and [efficacy] is attained accordingly."
Regarding what has been stated above together with the mantras: one should recite the mantra over each item according to its number and then burn it; this is called "reciting the mantras together.
When Mārīcī had finished expounding this method, the World-Honored One approved, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"What you have now spoken, I also rejoice in, for it is able to benefit all sentient beings.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, he addressed the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, and the common people, saying:
"Any person who hears this Mārīcī-devī dhāraṇī spoken by the Buddha and receives and maintains it with a single mind shall not be harmed by any evils whatsoever."

"O bhikṣus, if there be anyone who can write it down, recite it, or uphold it—if they wear it in their topknot or within their robes and carry it with them—all evils shall completely disperse and retreat, and none shall dare to oppose them."
These four assemblies, along with the eight classes of beings including devas and nāgas, prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew; they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
*The Scripture of the Goddess Mārīcī*, one fascicle.

*The Dharma of the Goddess Puṇyavatī*, one fascicle. These were translated at the Jingxing Monastery by the monk Ānanda, Master of the Vinaya and Prātimokṣa from the Bodhi Temple in Central India, together with Master Kāśyapa and others, alongside Dharma Master Guṇabhadra, for circulation in the land of Tang.
At that time, the goddess Puṇyavatī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
For those who study this Dharma, I shall provide them with whatever they require—clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and other assets—so that they lack for nothing.”
“With the mind fixed in mindfulness, rejoicing day and night, one should contemplate these mantra verses with right mindfulness and resolve for bodhicitta.

If sentient beings have planted various roots of goodness in the presence of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, this reciter of mantras shall, for their sake, widely proclaim and disseminate this sublime sutra throughout Jambudvīpa so that it shall not be interrupted.”

Once these sentient beings have heard this mantra, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kalpas in future ages, they shall experience happiness among devas and humans, encounter these various Buddhas, and swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi; the sufferings of the three evil realms shall be completely exhausted without remainder.
“World-Honored One!

I have already planted various roots of goodness in the presence of the past Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, World-Honored One named Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakaparvatejorāja. Therefore, wherever I direct my thoughts or wherever I go, I cause immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to experience all manner of happiness; whether it be clothing, food and drink, the necessities of life, gold, silver, the seven treasures, pearls, lapis lazuli, coral, amber, jade, or conch shells—none shall lack for anything.”

"If there is anyone who can recite this subtle and wondrous divine mantra of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, and for my sake make offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; if they recite my name three times and make offerings of incense; and having made these offerings, further bestow upon me various flowers, perfumes, and exquisite delicacies, scattering them in all directions—then you should know that such a person will be able to gather together wealth and treasures."

By these causes and conditions, the essence of the earth increases, enabling all the devas to attain complete joy; the grains, sprouts, stalks, branches, leaves, and fruits that are sown flourish and thrive, and the tree deities rejoice as they produce immeasurable varieties of things.
"At that time, out of my compassionate regard for all sentient beings, I provided them with many necessities for life.
World-Honored One!

To the north of here, King Vaiśravaṇa has a city named Animanda; in that city there is a park named Puṇyapuṣpābhāsa. Within this park is a most excellent garden called Suvarṇadhvaja, made of the seven precious jewels and exceedingly wonderful; this is my constant place of residence."

"If there are those who wish to increase their wealth and treasures, such persons should thoroughly sweep and sprinkle their own dwelling place; they should bathe their bodies, put on fresh white garments, and anoint themselves with exquisite incense. Then, for my sake, they should sincerely recite the name of that Buddha, the World-Honored One Ratnakusuma-vaidūrya, three times, prostrating, making offerings, burning incense, and scattering flowers."

You should also recite the name of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* three times, make a sincere vow, and separately offer me incense, flowers, and various delicious foods, scattering and sprinkling them in all directions.
"At that time, when reciting these words and phrases, one should form the mudrā of the body of Puṇyavatī and chant the Great Body Mantra.

Hook the two ring fingers together at their tips within the palms; extend the two little fingers straight upward with their tips separated by one inch; extend the two middle fingers straight upward with their tips touching; place the two index fingers upon the second joints of the backs of the two middle fingers; and extend the two thumbs side-by-side straight upward, moving the index fingers back and forth."
The mantra says:
"Pāripūtraṇe cāri samantata."
